2027-01-01.title: The Naming of our Lord · New Year's Day
2027-01-01.alt: Feast of the Naming of our Lord, eight days after Yaldo. New Year begins. Also the World Day of Peace in the universal Church.
2027-01-01.verse: After eight days had passed, it was time to circumcise the child; and he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
theo: On the eighth day after his birth the Child was circumcised according to the Law and given his name: Jesus, “the name given by the angel before he was conceived”. The Son of God enters fully into the covenant of his people and receives a name that is a mission: Yeshua, “the Lord saves”. As the angel told Joseph: “you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins” (Matthew 1:21).

At the start of a new year the Church gives us not a resolution but a Name. St Peter would later proclaim: “There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved” (Acts 4:12). Every year, every plan, every fear can be placed under this Name.

St Paul's reading tells us how to begin anew: “put away your former way of life, your old self… and clothe yourselves with the new self, created according to the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness” (Ephesians 4:22–24). A new calendar does not make a new person; Christ does. The New Year is a chance to put on Christ again.

Luke also says that Mary and Joseph brought the Child to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, offering the sacrifice of the poor, “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons”. The Holy Family begins every new stage by offering it to God. So may we offer this year to him.
conn: The eighth day.
Circumcision on the eighth day (Genesis 17:12) marked entry into Abraham's covenant. For Christians the eighth day became the day of the Resurrection and of the new creation.
Joshua and Jesus.
Jesus is the same name as Joshua, who led Israel into the promised land (Joshua 1:1–9). Jesus leads us into the true promised land.
The name above every name.
Paul sings that God gave Christ “the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend” (Philippians 2:9–10).
The offering of the poor.
The two birds (Leviticus 12:8) show that the Holy Family was poor. The Son of God was born among the poor.
altar: We begin the new year at the altar, where the Name of Jesus is invoked over bread and wine and he becomes present. To receive Holy Communion on the first day of the year is to place the whole year in his hands.
outline: New Year greetings: what do people usually wish for? Health, wealth, success.
Point 1 · A Name, not a wish
Jesus: “the Lord saves”. Begin the year under his Name.
Point 2 · Put on the new self
Ephesians 4: a new year needs a new heart, not only a new calendar.
Like Mary and Joseph presenting the Child, offer the year to God.
World Day of Peace: pray and work for peace in families and nations.
“Jesus, I begin this year in your Name.”
live: Begin each day with the Name
Begin each morning this year with the sign of the cross and the prayer “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me.”
One old habit to put off (Ephesians 4:22)
Name one habit of the “old self” to leave behind this year, and one virtue to put on.
Bless the house
Ask the priest to bless your home during the season of Denho, or bless it yourselves with prayer and holy water.
fathers: St Bernard of Clairvaux
The name of Jesus is light, food and medicine: “Jesus is honey in the mouth, music in the ear, a song of joy in the heart” (Sermons on the Song of Songs 15).
St Ephrem the Syrian
He praises the Name of the Son, sweet to those who love him, and the circumcision of the Lord who fulfilled the Law in himself (Hymns on the Nativity).
magis: Catechism 430–435
Jesus means “God saves”; the name of Jesus contains everything; it is at the heart of Christian prayer.
Catechism 527
The circumcision of Jesus is the sign of his incorporation into Abraham's descendants and prefigures Christian Baptism.
Message for the World Day of Peace
Each year on 1 January the Pope issues a message for peace; read it on vatican.va (see Papal documents).
saints: 2 Jan: Mar Baselios and Mar Gregory; name day of our Major Archbishop-Catholicos Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis. 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara.
2027-01-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, at your Naming you received the Name that saves. We begin this year in your Name: forgive our past, clothe us with the new self, bless our families and our work, and give peace to our world. Amen.

2027-01-03.title: Second Sunday after Yaldo
readings: The boy Samuel grows before the Lord
They shall mount up with wings like eagles
Here is the Lamb of God
2027-01-03.alt: Season of Yaldo–Denho. Denho, the Baptism of our Lord, is on Wednesday 6 January.
2027-01-03.verse: Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
theo: Between Yaldo and Denho the Church listens to John the Baptist. He sees Jesus coming and cries: “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!” The Child of Bethlehem is the Lamb who will be offered for us. John adds: “I myself have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.” Christmas joy is joined to the purpose of Christ's coming: to take away sin.

In the evening Gospel John is very practical. The crowds ask, “What then should we do?” He answers: “Whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none; and whoever has food must do likewise.” Tax collectors must be honest; soldiers must not extort. Conversion is not only a feeling; it bears fruit in the way we use money, power and possessions.

The Old Testament readings show children growing before God: Joseph loved by his father and given a long robe; the boy Samuel growing “in the presence of the LORD”, his mother bringing him a little robe each year. Hebrews remembers Moses, who chose “to share ill-treatment with the people of God rather than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin”.

Isaiah gives the promise for the new year: “Those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary.” Those who follow the Lamb do not run on their own strength.
conn: The Lamb.
The Passover lamb (Exodus 12) and the servant “like a lamb that is led to the slaughter” (Isaiah 53:7) are fulfilled in Jesus, the Lamb of God (John 1:29; Revelation 5:6).
Robes.
Joseph's robe and Samuel's little robe are signs of a parent's love; in Baptism we are clothed with Christ (Galatians 3:27).
Love in deed.
“Let us love, not in word or speech, but in truth and action” (1 John 3:18) is the same lesson as John's “two coats”.
Moses' choice.
Moses refused Pharaoh's palace for God's people; Christ left heaven's glory for us.
altar: Before Holy Communion the priest raises the holy Mysteries; in many liturgies we hear John's words: “Behold the Lamb of God.” The One John pointed to by the Jordan is the One we receive at the altar.
outline: Ask: what did we receive at Christmas? What did we give?
The Child of Yaldo is the Lamb who takes away sin.
Two coats, honest work, no extortion: conversion in practice.
Joseph, Samuel, Moses: let children grow in God's presence.
New strength for the new year for those who wait on the Lord.
“Behold the Lamb; and share your second coat.”
live: Share your second coat (Luke 3:11)
Give away one good item of clothing or food this week to someone who needs it.
Honest in work (Luke 3:13)
Check one area of your work or business for honesty and fairness.
Prepare for Denho
Come to the Denho Qurbono on Wednesday and renew your baptismal promises.
fathers: St Cyril of Alexandria
One Lamb died for all, to gather the whole flock of humanity to God the Father; one for all, that all might be subject to God (Commentary on John, Book 2).
St Ambrose of Milan
On “whoever has two coats”: mercy is the fullness of the virtues; it is required of all, rich and poor, according to what each has (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke 2).
magis: Catechism 608
John the Baptist pointed to Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world: the Suffering Servant and the Paschal Lamb.
Catechism 1434–1435
Interior conversion is expressed in fasting, prayer and almsgiving, reconciliation, and care for the poor.
Catechism 2443–2447
Love for the poor; giving to the needy is a work of justice.
saints: 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. 6 Jan (Wednesday): Denho, the Baptism of our Lord; Holy Qurbono for the people. 7 Jan: Exaltation of St John the Baptist. 8 Jan: St Stephen, the first martyr (as in the 2025–26 lectionary).
2027-01-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, have mercy on us. Make our conversion bear fruit in sharing, honesty and love, and renew our strength in this new year, that we may run and not be weary. Amen.

2027-01-06.title: Denho · The Baptism of our Lord
readings: You are my Son, the Beloved
Rebekah gives water at the well
The river flowing from the Temple
Draw water from the wells of salvation
Baptised in the name of the Lord Jesus
The water of rebirth and renewal
The Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan
2027-01-06.alt: Denho, the Baptism of our Lord: a day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people. In many parishes the waters are solemnly blessed.
2027-01-06.verse: This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.
theo: Denho means “rising” or “manifestation”. At the Jordan the hidden Child of Bethlehem is revealed to the world. When Jesus comes up from the water, “the heavens were opened to him and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him. And a voice from heaven said, ‘This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.’” For the first time the whole Holy Trinity is manifested: the Father speaks, the Son stands in the water, the Spirit descends.

John protests: “I need to be baptized by you.” Jesus answers: “Let it be so now; for it is proper for us in this way to fulfill all righteousness.” The sinless One goes down into the waters of repentance with sinners. He does not need to be cleansed; he cleanses the waters. The Fathers say that by his Baptism Christ sanctified the waters for our Baptism.

The Old Testament readings are full of water: Rebekah drawing water for a stranger and his camels; water filling the dry valley; Ezekiel's river flowing from the Temple, where “everything will live where the river goes”; Isaiah's promise: “With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.” All these streams flow into the Jordan, and from the Jordan into our baptismal font.

St Paul tells Titus: “the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all”, and God saved us “through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit”. Denho is our feast too. In Baptism the Father said to each of us, “You are my beloved child”, and the Spirit came to dwell in us. Today we renew that grace.
conn: The Trinity revealed.
Father, Son and Holy Spirit appear together at the Jordan, as the Son later sends the apostles to baptise “in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 28:19).
The dove.
The dove over the waters recalls the Spirit hovering over the waters at creation (Genesis 1:2) and the dove of the flood (Genesis 8:11): a new creation begins.
The river of life.
Ezekiel's river (47:1–12) flows again in Revelation 22:1, “the river of the water of life… flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb”.
Baptism in the name of Jesus.
In Acts 19 Paul baptises disciples who knew only John's baptism, and the Holy Spirit comes upon them: Christian Baptism gives the Spirit.
altar: The Spirit who descended on Jesus at the Jordan descends on the bread and wine at every Holy Qurbono. The water mixed with the wine in the chalice recalls our Baptism and our union with Christ.
outline: Recall our own baptism day: who brought us, who were our godparents?
The Trinity at the Jordan: the Father's voice, the Son, the Spirit.
The sinless One goes down among sinners; he cleanses the waters for us.
Rebekah, Ezekiel, Isaiah: water as God's gift of life.
Baptism makes us children of God. Renew the baptismal promises.
“In Christ, I too am the Father's beloved child.”
live: Know your baptism day
Find out the date of your Baptism and keep it each year with a prayer of thanks.
Use holy water
Take home the blessed water of Denho; bless yourself and your children every night.
Renew the promises
Pray the Creed slowly today as the renewal of your baptismal faith.
fathers: St Gregory of Nazianzus
“Christ is baptised: let us go down with him, that we may also rise with him.” He comes to sanctify the Jordan for our sake (Oration 39, On the Holy Lights).
St Ephrem the Syrian
“Come down, my brothers, put on from the waters the Holy Spirit.” In his Hymns on the Epiphany he sings of the Lord who went down into the river and made the waters a womb of new birth.
magis: Catechism 535–537
The baptism of Jesus is his acceptance of his mission as the Suffering Servant; the Spirit and the Father's voice reveal him. Through Baptism the Christian is sacramentally assimilated to Jesus.
Catechism 1223–1225
The Lord's baptism and his Passover are the sources of Christian Baptism.
Catechism 1213
Baptism is the gateway to life in the Spirit; by it we are freed from sin and reborn as children of God.
saints: 7 Jan: Exaltation of St John the Baptist. 8 Jan: St Stephen, the first martyr. Confirm in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2027-01-06.prayer: Eternal Father, at the Jordan you revealed your beloved Son and sent your Holy Spirit upon him. Renew in us the grace of our Baptism, make us live as your beloved children, and let the river of your life flow through our homes and our Church. Amen.

2027-01-10.title: First Sunday after Denho
readings: The burning bush: I AM WHO I AM
The Lord has comforted his people
Chosen in Christ before the foundation of the world
The call of the first disciples
2027-01-10.verse: Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.
theo: After his Baptism Jesus begins his public ministry in Galilee. Matthew sees Isaiah fulfilled: “the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light.” Jesus' first preaching is short: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.” His first action is to call people: by the Sea of Galilee he sees Simon and Andrew, James and John at work, and says, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” “Immediately they left their nets and followed him.”

The Old Testament readings show God calling people in the middle of ordinary work. Moses was keeping his father-in-law's sheep when he saw the bush that burned and was not consumed, and heard: “Remove the sandals from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.” God reveals his name, “I AM WHO I AM”, and sends Moses to free his people. Jacob too was a shepherd, and God blessed the work of his hands.

St Paul says that this call did not begin by the lake. God “chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love” (Ephesians 1:4). And Acts shows what the call produces: a community that “devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers” (Acts 2:42).

Denho is the season of the manifestation of Christ. He is manifested not only at the Jordan, but every time someone leaves their nets and follows him. Each of us is called: to holiness, to a vocation, to bring others to Christ.
conn: Called at work.
Moses with the flock, David with the sheep, the apostles with their nets: God calls people in the middle of daily work.
Light in Galilee.
Matthew 4:16 fulfils Isaiah 9:1–2, read at Yaldo: the light born in Bethlehem now shines in Galilee.
Fishers of people.
Jeremiah 16:16 speaks of God sending “many fishermen”; Jesus turns fishermen into his messengers.
The first parish.
Acts 2:42–47 is the model of every parish: teaching, fellowship, Eucharist, prayer, sharing.
altar: The first Christians were faithful to “the breaking of bread”. The Holy Qurbono is where the call to follow Jesus is renewed each Sunday: we leave our nets for an hour and come to the One who calls us.
outline: Ask: what are the “nets” that keep us busy?
Jesus begins where people live and work.
Moses at the burning bush: God calls in ordinary places. Reverence before the holy.
Immediate response. What do I need to leave to follow him?
Acts 2:42: teaching, fellowship, Qurbono, prayer. Pray for vocations.
“Lord, I leave my nets; I will follow you.”
live: Pray for vocations
Pray each day this week for priests, religious and missionaries from your parish.
Bring one person
Invite one person to come with you to Holy Qurbono or a prayer meeting.
Reverence in church (Exodus 3:5)
Keep silence and reverence in the church before and after Qurbono.
fathers: St John Chrysostom
He admires the obedience of the fishermen: they did not delay or say “let us go home first”, but left everything at once, as Elisha left his oxen to follow Elijah (Homilies on Matthew 14).
St Gregory of Nyssa
On the burning bush: the fire that does not consume the bush foreshadows the Virgin who bore the Light without harm, and the mystery of God's presence (Life of Moses II).
magis: Catechism 787–789
From the beginning Jesus associated his disciples with his own life; the Church is the communion with Jesus.
God reveals his name to Moses: “I AM”; the name expresses God's faithfulness.
Christus Vivit 248–258
Pope Francis on vocation: every life is a call to follow Christ and to serve.
saints: 14 Jan: St Devasahayam, martyr of Travancore. 15 Jan: Commemoration of Mary, Mother of God, for the seeds (as in the 2025–26 lectionary). 17 Jan: St Antony of Egypt.
2027-01-10.prayer: Lord Jesus, light of Galilee, you called fishermen to follow you and made them fishers of people. Call us again today: give us courage to leave our nets, reverence before your holiness, and joy in your Church. Raise up many vocations from our families. Amen.

2027-01-17.title: Second Sunday after Denho
readings: Jesus returns to Galilee in the power of the Spirit
I am the Lord who sanctifies you
Wisdom at the beginning of creation
He shall feed his flock in the strength of the Lord
Look to the rock from which you were hewn
Be holy, for I am holy
2027-01-17.alt: Season of Denho. The Nineveh fast (three days) is from Monday 18 to Wednesday 20 January 2027.
2027-01-17.verse: Very truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
theo: Philip finds Nathanael and tells him: “We have found him about whom Moses in the law and also the prophets wrote, Jesus son of Joseph from Nazareth.” Nathanael is sceptical: “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip does not argue. He says: “Come and see.” That is still the best way to bring someone to Christ: not debate, but an invitation to meet him.

Jesus knows Nathanael before they meet: “I saw you under the fig tree.” Nathanael's doubt turns into faith: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!” And Jesus promises more: “You will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.” Jacob dreamed of a ladder between heaven and earth (Genesis 28:12); Jesus says he himself is that ladder, the meeting place of God and humanity.

Proverbs presents Wisdom, present with God “at the beginning of his work”, delighting in creation; “whoever finds me finds life”. The Fathers saw here the eternal Son, the Wisdom of God. Micah promises the ruler from Bethlehem who “shall feed his flock in the strength of the LORD”. Peter draws the consequence: “as he who called you is holy, be holy yourselves in all your conduct.”

Tomorrow the Nineveh fast begins. Jonah preached in Nineveh and the whole city repented in sackcloth and ashes. The three days of fasting prepare us for the Great Fast. Like Nathanael, we are invited to come and see; like the Ninevites, to turn back to God with our whole heart.
conn: Jacob's ladder.
John 1:51 recalls Genesis 28:12: Christ is the true Bethel, the house of God and gate of heaven.
Wisdom made flesh.
Proverbs 8:22–31 speaks of Wisdom present at creation; John 1:1–3 and Colossians 1:15–17 see in Christ the Word through whom all things were made.
The rock.
“Look to the rock from which you were hewn” (Isaiah 51:1): our faith has roots in Abraham and Sarah, and in the apostles.
Holy as God is holy.
Leviticus 22:32 (“I am the LORD; I sanctify you”) is the root of 1 Peter 1:16: “You shall be holy, for I am holy.”
altar: “You will see heaven opened.” At every Holy Qurbono heaven opens over the altar: the angels join our worship and the Son of Man comes down to us in his Body and Blood.
outline: Ask: who first invited you to know Jesus?
The way of evangelisation: invitation and encounter, not argument.
“I saw you under the fig tree.” God knows us before we know him.
Christ is Jacob's ladder; the Qurbono is heaven on earth.
Three days of fasting, prayer and repentance, as preparation for the Great Fast.
live: Say “Come and see”
Invite one friend, colleague or relative to Qurbono, a retreat or a prayer meeting.
Keep the Nineveh fast
Monday to Wednesday: fasting, the special prayers, and confession of sins.
Be holy in one thing (1 Peter 1:15)
Choose one area of conduct (speech, honesty, purity) to make holy this week.
fathers: St Augustine
Nathanael under the fig tree: Christ saw him before Philip called him, as he sees each of us under the shade of sin before grace calls us (Tractates on John 7).
St Athanasius of Alexandria
Proverbs 8 speaks of the Son, the Wisdom of the Father, through whom all things were made, and who became man for our sake (Against the Arians II).
magis: Evangelii Gaudium 127–129
Evangelisation person to person: a friendly conversation that invites the other to encounter Christ.
Catechism 1438
Seasons of penance in the liturgical year are intense moments of the Church's penitential practice.
Catechism 2013–2014
All the faithful are called to the fullness of Christian life and to holiness.
saints: 17 Jan: St Antony of Egypt. 18–20 Jan: the Nineveh fast. 18–25 Jan: the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity. 20 Jan: St Sebastian. 21 Jan: St Agnes.
2027-01-17.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw Nathanael under the fig tree and opened heaven before him. Help us to say “Come and see” to those who do not know you, and in these days of the Nineveh fast turn our hearts back to you, that we may be holy as you are holy. Amen.

2027-01-24.title: Kohne Sunday · Commemoration of the Departed Priests
readings: Aaron anointed for an everlasting covenant
Paul's farewell to the elders of Ephesus
2027-01-24.alt: Kohne Sunday: the Church remembers the priests who have died. In the 2025–26 lectionary this Sunday was also Catholicos Day.
2027-01-24.verse: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.
theo: Before the Great Fast the Malankara Church keeps three Sundays of remembrance. The first is Kohne Sunday, the commemoration of the departed priests (kohne in Syriac). We remember the bishops and priests who baptised us, taught us, absolved our sins, celebrated the Holy Qurbono for us, and buried our dead. Hebrews tells us: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.”

The readings recall the death of Israel's great servants. Aaron, the first high priest, dies on Mount Hor, and Moses places his vestments on his son Eleazar (Numbers 20:28): the priesthood continues though the priest dies. Joshua dies after leading the people into the land. Sirach remembers Aaron anointed “for an everlasting covenant… to minister to the Lord and serve as priest and bless his people in his name” (Sirach 45:15).

In Acts Paul says farewell to the elders of Ephesus: “Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son.” And he reminds them of the Lord's words: “It is more blessed to give than to receive.” The Gospel asks the question every priest will be asked: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give them their food at the proper time? Blessed is that servant whom his master will find at work when he arrives.”

We pray today for the departed priests, that the Lord who called them may forgive their weaknesses and say to them: “Well done, good servant!” (Luke 19:17). And we pray for our living priests, and for new vocations. “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever” (Hebrews 13:8): priests pass, but the one High Priest remains.
conn: Vestments passed on.
Aaron's garments placed on Eleazar (Numbers 20:28): the priesthood does not die with the priest. In the Church the one priesthood of Christ continues through every generation.
The faithful servant.
Luke 19 and Matthew 24: priests are stewards, not owners; they will give an account.
Paul's farewell.
Acts 20 is the model of a pastor's last words: I did not shrink from declaring the whole purpose of God; I coveted no one's silver or gold.
One High Priest.
Hebrews 13:8–16: Christ the same yesterday, today and for ever; our sacrifice of praise continues his.
altar: Every Holy Qurbono offered today in the world is offered by hands that will one day be still. Through them the one Priest, Christ, offers his one sacrifice. Today we offer the Qurbono for the priests who once stood at this altar for us.
outline: Name the priests who baptised you, gave you First Communion, married you, buried your parents.
Gratitude for the priests who served us.
Aaron's vestments on Eleazar: Christ's priesthood outlives every priest.
The faithful and wise servant: a word for priests and for every Christian steward.
For the departed, for the living, for vocations.
live: Pray for departed priests
Pray by name for the priests who served your family, living and dead.
Thank your parish priest
Tell your parish priest one thing you are grateful for.
Pray for vocations
Pray daily for one young person from your parish to answer God's call.
fathers: St John Chrysostom

On the priesthood: the priest stands at the altar as a minister of heavenly things; the dignity is great, and so is the responsibility, for he will answer for the souls entrusted to him (On the Priesthood III).
St Gregory the Great
The good shepherd is known by his care for the flock: he must be near to each by compassion and above all by contemplation (Pastoral Rule II).
magis: Presbyterorum Ordinis 2–3
Priests share in the priesthood of Christ; taken from among the people, they are set apart for the people, to offer sacrifice and forgive sins in Christ's name.
Catechism 1547–1553
The ministerial priesthood is at the service of the common priesthood; the priest acts in the person of Christ the Head.
Catechism 1032
The Church prays and offers the Eucharistic sacrifice for the dead.
saints: 25 Jan: the Conversion of St Paul; the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity ends. 26 Jan: Republic Day of India. 28 Jan: St Thomas Aquinas. 31 Jan: St John Bosco.
2027-01-24.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, eternal High Priest, we remember before you the bishops and priests who served your people and have gone to their rest. Forgive their weaknesses, reward their labours, and give them a place of light. Keep our living priests faithful, and raise up new labourers for your harvest. Amen.

2027-01-31.title: Aneede Sunday · Commemoration of the Departed Faithful
readings: Jacob is gathered to his people
New heavens and a new earth
We will be with the Lord for ever
The dead will hear the voice of the Son of God
2027-01-31.alt: Aneede Sunday: the Church remembers all the faithful departed. The Great Fast begins next Sunday. (In 2025–26 this Sunday was also Malankara Catholic Children's League Day.)
2027-01-31.verse: Very truly, I tell you, anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life.
theo: Last Sunday we remembered the departed priests; today, Aneede Sunday, we remember all the faithful departed: our parents and grandparents, brothers and sisters, children and friends. The Church does not forget them. Before we enter the Great Fast, we gather them in prayer, because Lent leads to Easter, the victory of Christ over death.

Jesus says: “The hour is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live… all who are in their graves will hear his voice and will come out.” St Paul writes to the Thessalonians so “that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope.” Christian grief is real, but it is grief with hope: “so we will be with the Lord forever.”

The reading from 2 Maccabees shows that God's people prayed for the dead even before Christ. Judas Maccabeus took up a collection for a sin offering for the fallen, “for if he were not expecting that those who had fallen would rise again, it would have been superfluous and foolish to pray for the dead”. From the beginning the Church has prayed for the departed and offered the Holy Qurbono for them, that they may be purified and enter the joy of God.

The evening Gospel reminds us how we will be judged: “I was hungry and you gave me food… just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.” The best way to honour our dead is to pray for them and to live in such a way that, when our turn comes, we too may hear: “Come, you that are blessed by my Father.”
conn: Gathered to his people.
Jacob “breathed his last, and was gathered to his people” (Genesis 49:33): death is a gathering, not an ending.
Prayer for the dead.
2 Maccabees 12:45 is the Old Testament root of the Church's prayer for the departed (CCC 1032).
Hezekiah's song.
“You have held back my life from the pit of destruction, for you have cast all my sins behind your back” (Isaiah 38:17): God's mercy reaches beyond death.
New heavens and a new earth.
2 Peter 3:13 and Revelation 21:1: our hope is not only for souls but for a renewed creation and the resurrection of the body.
altar: In every Holy Qurbono, in the Thubden, the Church remembers the faithful departed by name. Today we offer the Qurbono for all our dead: the Body and Blood of the risen Lord are the pledge of their resurrection and ours.
outline: Invite the people to name silently those they have lost.
1 Thessalonians 4: not as those who have no hope.
Point 2 · Why we pray for the dead
2 Maccabees 12; the Church's tradition; the Qurbono for the departed.
Matthew 25: the hungry, the stranger, the sick, the prisoner.
Lent is the journey to the Resurrection.
“We will be with the Lord forever.”
live: Pray for your dead
Write the names of your departed family members and pray for them each day this week; offer a Qurbono for them.
Visit the cemetery
Visit the graves of your family, clean them, and pray there.
Do one work of mercy (Matthew 25)
Feed, visit or clothe someone this week in memory of a departed loved one.
fathers: St Augustine
His mother Monica asked as she was dying: “Lay this body anywhere; only this I ask of you, that you remember me at the altar of the Lord, wherever you may be” (Confessions IX, 11).
St John Chrysostom
“Let us help and commemorate them… Why would you doubt that our offerings for the dead bring them some consolation?” (Homilies on 1 Corinthians 41).
magis: Catechism 1030–1032
Those who die in God's grace but still imperfectly purified undergo purification; the Church commends prayer, the Eucharistic sacrifice, almsgiving and works of penance for them.
Catechism 1680–1690
The Christian funeral and the communion of saints with the departed.
Lumen Gentium 49–50
The union of the pilgrim Church with those who have died in Christ is not broken, but strengthened by the sharing of spiritual goods.
saints: 31 Jan: St John Bosco. 2 Feb (Tuesday): Mayaltho, the Entrance of our Lord into the Temple. 3 Feb: Mar Simon and Morth Hanna (as in the 2025–26 lectionary). 4 Feb: St John de Britto.
2027-01-31.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you are the resurrection and the life. Remember all our departed brothers and sisters, our parents, relatives, friends and benefactors, and those whom no one remembers. Forgive their sins, give them eternal rest, and let perpetual light shine upon them. Amen.

2027-01-02.title: Saturday after New Year · Mar Baselios and Mar Gregorios
readings: The Lord's servant must be kindly to everyone
You must be born from above
2027-01-02.alt: Season of Yaldo and Denho. Name day of Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis Catholicos. Anniversary of the erection of the Eparchy of Mavelikara (2007). Mar Macarios the Egyptian.
2027-01-02.verse: Jesus answered, “Very truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.
theo: Today the Church remembers Mar Baselios (St Basil the Great) and Mar Gregorios (St Gregory Nazianzen), friends and bishops of Cappadocia who defended faith in the Holy Trinity, and whose names are borne by our Catholicos and many of our bishops. It is the name day of Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis Catholicos; we pray for him and for the Eparchy of Mavelikara, erected on this day in 2007.

In the Gospel Nicodemus comes to Jesus by night. Jesus tells him: “no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.” A few days before Denho, the feast of Jesus' baptism, we are reminded of our own: a new birth from above. Jesus also says that the Son of Man must be lifted up, as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness. Paul tells Timothy that the Lord's servant “must not be quarrelsome but kindly to everyone, an apt teacher, patient.” Basil and Gregory were exactly this: firm in the truth, gentle with people.
outline: Ask: what does it mean to be born again?
Basil, Gregory and every servant of the Lord.
live: Pray for our shepherds
Pray today for our Catholicos and the bishops of our Church.
Correct gently (2 Timothy 2:25)
If you must correct someone today, do it with gentleness.
2027-01-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, you call us to be born from above of water and the Spirit. Through the prayers of Mar Baselios and Mar Gregorios, keep our Catholicos and bishops faithful and gentle shepherds, and renew in us the grace of our Baptism. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbono is offered for the Catholicos and the bishops by name. Today we pray especially for Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis on his name day.

2027-01-04.title: Monday after the Second Sunday after Yaldo · Prophet Malachi; St Kuriakose Elias Chavara
readings: Without faith it is impossible to please God
2027-01-04.alt: Season of Yaldo and Denho. The feast of Denho is on Wednesday: remind the faithful.
2027-01-04.verse: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
theo: Hebrews begins its great chapter on faith with three ancient figures. Abel offered a more acceptable sacrifice; Enoch “pleased God” and was taken up; Noah, warned of things not yet seen, built an ark and saved his household. The principle is simple: “without faith it is impossible to please God, for whoever would approach him must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.” Faith is not a feeling but a life that trusts God's word and acts on it.

The Gospel gives the Beatitudes, the portrait of a life of faith: poor in spirit, mourning, meek, hungry for righteousness, merciful, pure in heart, peacemakers, persecuted. Today we remember the prophet Malachi, last of the prophets, who promised that “the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings”, and St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, a son of Kerala who lived the Beatitudes as priest, founder and teacher. Two days before Denho, they point us to the Sun that rises at the Jordan.
outline: Ask: who in your life lived the Beatitudes?
Point 2 · Blessed are the pure in heart
The Beatitudes as a way of life.
“Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.”
live: Choose one Beatitude
Choose one Beatitude and live it deliberately this week.
Learn from St Chavara
Read a short life of St Chavara with your family.
2027-01-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, Sun of righteousness, you taught us the Beatitudes and lived them perfectly. Through the prayers of the prophet Malachi and St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, give us a pure heart and a living faith, so that we may see God. Amen.
altar: The pure in heart will see God. In the Holy Qurbono we see him already under the veil of bread and wine; purity of heart prepares us to receive him.

2027-01-05.title: Tuesday after the Second Sunday after Yaldo · Eve of Denho
readings: Grow up in every way into Christ
2027-01-05.alt: Season of Yaldo and Denho. Anniversary of the erection of the Eparchy of St Mary, Queen of Peace, USA–Canada (2016). Tomorrow is Denho: a day of obligation.
2027-01-05.verse: Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not clothed like one of these.
theo: Paul says that the ascended Christ gave gifts to his Church, “some would be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors and teachers, to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up the body of Christ.” The goal is maturity: “speaking the truth in love, we must grow up in every way into him who is the head, into Christ.” Each member has a part; when each works properly, the body grows in love.

In the Gospel Jesus tells his disciples not to worry about food or clothing: look at the ravens, consider the lilies. God feeds and clothes them; how much more will he care for you, “you of little faith”. Today we remember the erection of our Eparchy in the USA and Canada in 2016: thousands of our families live far from Kerala, often under great pressure of work and money. The word of Jesus is for them too: your Father knows what you need. On the eve of Denho, let us lay our worries before the Father who will speak tomorrow at the Jordan: “This is my beloved Son.”
outline: Ask: what worries are you carrying into the new year?
The Father knows what you need.
live: Hand over a worry (Luke 12:22)
Name your biggest worry and entrust it to God in prayer tonight.
Pray for the diaspora
Call or message a relative or friend abroad and assure them of your prayers.
2027-01-05.prayer: Heavenly Father, you clothe the lilies and feed the ravens. Free us from anxious worry, help us grow into Christ by speaking the truth in love, and protect our families in every land, especially the faithful of our Eparchy in the USA and Canada. Amen.
altar: At every Qurbono the gifts of each member are gathered into one offering. Each of us has a place in the Body of Christ.

2027-01-07.title: Thursday after Denho · The Praise of St John the Baptist
readings: A servant of the gospel by the gift of God's grace
Among those born of women no one is greater than John
2027-01-07.verse: I tell you, among those born of women no one is greater than John; yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
theo: On the day after Denho the Syriac tradition praises the one who baptised the Lord. Jesus himself gives John's praise: “What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?” No, John was firm. “Someone dressed in soft robes?” No, he lived in poverty. “A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.” He is the messenger foretold to prepare the way. “Among those born of women no one is greater than John.”

And then a surprise: “yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.” John stood at the threshold; we, by Baptism, have entered. The grace of the Kingdom is greater than any human greatness. Paul calls himself “the very least of all the saints”, yet a servant of the Gospel “according to the gift of God's grace”. The mystery hidden for ages is now revealed: the Gentiles are fellow heirs in Christ. John prepared the way; we are sent to walk it.
outline: Ask: who is the greatest person you have ever met?
Point 3 · The least in the Kingdom
“Among those born of women no one is greater than John.”
live: Stand firm (Luke 7:24)
Refuse one compromise with the truth today.
Thank God for Baptism
Pray: thank you, Lord, for making me a child of your Kingdom.
2027-01-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, you praised John the Baptist, your messenger and the friend who baptised you. Make us firm as he was, simple as he was, and grateful for the grace of the Kingdom we have received in Baptism. Amen.
altar: John pointed to the Lamb of God. In the Holy Qurbono we receive that Lamb. The least in the Kingdom is fed with the Lord himself.

2027-01-08.title: Friday after Denho · Mar Stephanos, the First Martyr
readings: Devoted to the service of the saints
I send you prophets, sages and scribes
2027-01-08.alt: Season of Denho. Name day of Bishop Philipos Mar Stephanos.
2027-01-08.verse: While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Then he knelt down and cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” When he had said this, he died.
theo: In the days of Denho the Syriac Churches honour Mar Stephanos, the first martyr. After his great speech before the council, “filled with the Holy Spirit, he gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.” What the Baptist saw at the Jordan, the open heavens, Stephen sees at his death. They drag him out and stone him; he prays like his Master: “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit… Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” A young man named Saul stands by, guarding their coats.

Jesus had foretold it: “I send you prophets, sages, and scribes, some of whom you will kill and crucify.” Martyrdom is not failure; it is the Gospel lived to the end. Paul, once Saul, later praises the household of Stephanas, whose name means crown, for devoting themselves “to the service of the saints”. Today is the name day of Bishop Philipos Mar Stephanos; we pray for him and for all who serve. Stephen began as a deacon serving tables and ended with the crown of martyrdom: service and witness are one road.
outline: Ask: could you forgive someone who was hurting you at that very moment?
The household of Stephanas, the deacon's way.
“Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
live: Forgive (Acts 7:60)
Pray by name today for someone who has hurt you.
Serve the saints (1 Corinthians 16:15)
Offer one practical service in your parish this week.
2027-01-08.prayer: Lord Jesus, you stood at the right hand of God to receive your martyr Stephen. Give us his faith to see heaven open, his love to forgive our enemies, and his humility to serve. Bless Bishop Philipos Mar Stephanos on his name day. Amen.
altar: Stephen was a deacon. At every Qurbono the deacon serves at the altar and among the people; service at the altar and service of the poor belong together.

2027-01-09.title: Saturday after Denho
readings: Will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God?
You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition
2027-01-09.verse: You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition.
theo: The Pharisees notice that some of Jesus' disciples eat with unwashed hands, against “the tradition of the elders”. Jesus answers with Isaiah: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.” He does not despise tradition; the Church lives by Holy Tradition. He rejects the human customs that take the place of God's commandment and leave the heart untouched. The washing that matters is of the heart.

Paul faces a related question: if Israel was unfaithful, has God failed? “By no means! Although everyone is a liar, let God be proved true.” Our unfaithfulness does not cancel God's faithfulness. A few days after Denho, the feast of the Lord's baptism, we remember the washing God gave us in Baptism: not of hands but of hearts. Let our customs, fasts and devotions serve the love of God, not replace it.
outline: Ask: which of our customs help us love God, and which have become empty?
Our sin does not cancel his truth.
live: Examine a habit (Mark 7:8)
Look at one religious habit: is it still prayer from the heart?
Thank God for his faithfulness
Recall one time God was faithful when you were not.
2027-01-09.prayer: Faithful God, even when we are unfaithful, you remain true. Wash our hearts as you washed us in Baptism, and let all our customs and devotions spring from love for you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Before the anaphora the priest washes his hands and prays for purity of heart. The outward sign asks for the inward gift.

2027-01-11.title: Monday after the First Sunday after Denho · Mar Gregorios of Nyssa
readings: He gives the Spirit without measure
2027-01-11.verse: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation, who consoles us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to console those who are in any affliction with the consolation with which we ourselves are consoled by God.
theo: Paul opens his second letter to the Corinthians not with complaints about his sufferings, though they were many, but with a blessing: God is “the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation”. In Asia Paul had felt “the sentence of death”, and he learned to “rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead.” The comfort he received becomes comfort he can give. Our wounds, once consoled by God, become a ministry to others.

In the Gospel John the Baptist says of Jesus: “He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.” Today we remember Mar Gregorios of Nyssa, younger brother of Mar Baselios, a bishop and mystic who taught that the soul never stops growing toward God: each discovery opens a greater longing. The Spirit given without measure keeps drawing us further into the endless love of God.
outline: Ask: who consoled you in your hardest time?
Point 1 · The God of all consolation
Point 2 · Relying on God who raises the dead
“The Father of mercies and the God of all consolation.”
live: Console someone (2 Corinthians 1:4)
Visit or call someone who is suffering, and share how God helped you.
Grow in prayer
Add five minutes to your daily prayer this week.
2027-01-11.prayer: Father of mercies and God of all consolation, you comfort us in every affliction. Teach us to rely on you who raise the dead, fill us with the Spirit without measure, and through the prayers of Mar Gregorios let us grow without end in your love. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono we receive the consolation of the risen Christ, so that we may carry it to those who suffer.

2027-01-12.title: Tuesday after the First Sunday after Denho · Mar Thevodosios the Abbot
readings: The light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ
It is lawful to do good on the sabbath
2027-01-12.alt: Season of Denho. Name day of Bishop Yoohanon Mar Theodosius.
2027-01-12.verse: For it is the God who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
theo: Paul describes his ministry as pure light: “we do not proclaim ourselves; we proclaim Jesus Christ as Lord and ourselves as your slaves for Jesus' sake.” The same God who said at creation, “Let light shine out of darkness”, has shone in our hearts “to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.” In Denho we contemplate that face: the glory of God is not far away but shines in a human face.

In the synagogue a man with a withered hand is placed before Jesus as a test: is it lawful to cure on the sabbath? Jesus answers: you would lift your sheep out of a pit; “How much more valuable is a human being than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the sabbath.” He says, “Stretch out your hand,” and it is restored. Today we remember Mar Thevodosios the Abbot, who built monasteries with houses for the sick, the old and the poor beside them: prayer and works of mercy in one place. We pray for Bishop Yoohanon Mar Theodosius on his name day.
outline: Ask: what does the face of a loving person reveal?
The servant points to the Lord.
Point 3 · Do good on the sabbath
“It is lawful to do good on the sabbath.”
live: Do good on Sunday (Matthew 12:12)
After Qurbono this Sunday, visit a sick or lonely person.
Point to Christ (2 Corinthians 4:5)
In one conversation today, speak of Christ, not of your achievements.
2027-01-12.prayer: God of light, you said “Let light shine out of darkness” and shone in our hearts in the face of Jesus. Let us proclaim him, not ourselves, and stretch out our hands to do good. Through the prayers of Mar Thevodosios, unite prayer and mercy in our lives. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the face of Christ shines for us in the mysteries. From the altar we go out to do good on the Lord's day.

2027-01-13.title: Wednesday after the First Sunday after Denho
readings: Prayers for everyone; one mediator, Christ Jesus
2027-01-13.verse: Why do you see the speck in your neighbor's eye, but do not notice the log in your own eye?
theo: Paul asks Timothy for a Church that prays for everyone: “supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone, for kings and all who are in high positions.” Why everyone? Because God “desires everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. For there is one God; there is also one mediator between God and humankind, Christ Jesus, himself human.” The Church's prayer is as wide as God's desire to save.

Jesus forbids the opposite attitude: “Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.” With humour he describes a man with a log in his eye trying to remove a speck from his brother's. This is not a ban on all discernment; it is a ban on condemning, on the harsh eye that sees others' faults and never its own. Intercession and judging cannot live in the same heart: we cannot pray sincerely for someone while condemning him.
outline: Ask: for whom do you find it hard to pray?
Point 3 · The log and the speck
Look first at your own eye.
“Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.”
live: Pray for leaders (1 Timothy 2:2)
Pray today by name for our national and state leaders.
Remove your log (Matthew 7:5)
Before criticising anyone today, name one fault of your own.
2027-01-13.prayer: Lord Jesus, one mediator between God and humankind, you desire all to be saved. Widen my prayer to include everyone, and free me from judging others, so that I may first see my own faults. Amen.
altar: The intercessions of the Holy Qurbono include the whole world: rulers, the sick, travellers, the departed. There we learn to pray for everyone.

2027-01-14.title: Thursday after the First Sunday after Denho · The Forty Martyrs of Sinai; St Devasahayam
readings: Justified by his grace as a gift
Do not fear those who kill the body
2027-01-14.verse: But even the hairs of your head are all counted. Do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.
theo: Paul states the heart of the Gospel: “all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; they are now justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.” No one earns salvation; it is a gift received by faith. This frees us from fear of failing and from pride in succeeding. Everything we are before God is grace.

Jesus tells his friends: “do not fear those who kill the body, and after that can do nothing more.” Five sparrows sold for two pennies, yet not one is forgotten by God; “even the hairs of your head are all counted.” Today the Syriac tradition remembers the Forty Martyrs of Sinai, monks killed by raiders while praying, and the Church in India honours St Devasahayam, who gave his life for Christ in 1752. They feared God, and so they feared nothing else.
outline: Ask: what do you fear most?
All have sinned; all can be saved.
Those who kill the body can do no more.
“Do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.”
live: Receive grace (Romans 3:24)
Thank God today for one gift you did not earn.
Courage for Christ
Do not hide your faith in one situation today.
2027-01-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, you justify us by grace and tell us not to fear. Through the prayers of the Forty Martyrs of Sinai and St Devasahayam, give us courage to witness and trust in your care, for you count every hair of our head. Amen.
altar: The martyrs offered their lives with Christ. At every Qurbono we offer ourselves with him, trusting the Father who counts every hair of our heads.

2027-01-15.title: Friday after the First Sunday after Denho · Commemoration of Mary, Mother of God, for the Seeds
readings: God supplies seed to the sower
2027-01-15.alt: Season of Denho. Anniversary of the erection of the Eparchy of Muvattupuzha (2003).
2027-01-15.verse: He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
theo: The Syriac Churches keep in January a commemoration of the Mother of God for the seeds: at the season of sowing, farmers brought their seed to church to be blessed, entrusting the year's harvest to the prayers of Mary. Paul's words fit perfectly: “the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.” And: “He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed.” Generosity is sowing; God gives the growth.

In the Gospel Mary receives the shepherds' story and “treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.” Mary is the good soil where the Word is sown and bears fruit. Today we pray for farmers and for all who work the land, for a good harvest and fair prices, and for the Eparchy of Muvattupuzha on its anniversary. Let our hearts, like Mary's, receive the seed of God's word, and let our hands sow generously.
outline: Ask: what are you sowing in your life this year?
live: Pray for farmers
Pray today for farmers, and buy something directly from a local farmer this week.
Sow generously (2 Corinthians 9:7)
Give cheerfully to one person in need this week.
2027-01-15.prayer: God who gives seed to the sower and bread for food, through the prayers of the Mother of God bless the seed of our farmers and the work of our hands. Make our hearts good soil for your word, as Mary's was, and make us cheerful givers. Amen.
altar: Bread and wine come from seed sown in the earth. At the Qurbono, the fruit of the earth and work of human hands becomes the Body and Blood of Christ.

2027-01-16.title: Saturday after the First Sunday after Denho · The Bonds of St Peter
readings: Remember your leaders; Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever
2027-01-16.alt: Season of Denho. Commemoration of Bishop Geevarghese Mar Divannasios (2018). Alternative Gospels: John 10:11–18; John 14:1–6; John 15:9–17.
2027-01-16.verse: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
theo: Hebrews asks us to “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.” Today we remember two such leaders: St Peter, whose chains in prison (Acts 12) the Church honours, and Bishop Geevarghese Mar Divannasios, a shepherd of our own Church who died in 2018. Leaders pass; the one they served remains: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”

Jesus asks: “Who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give the other slaves their allowance of food at the proper time? Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives.” Every Christian is a steward of something: family, work, talents, a parish ministry. Hebrews adds the worship that pleases God: a “sacrifice of praise… the fruit of lips that confess his name”, and doing good and sharing what we have.
outline: Ask: which leader in faith do you most remember?
Found at work when he comes.
“Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
live: Remember a leader (Hebrews 13:7)
Pray today for a priest, bishop or teacher who formed your faith, living or departed.
Be faithful in small things (Matthew 24:45)
Do today's duties well, as for the Lord.
2027-01-16.prayer: Lord Jesus, the same yesterday, today and forever, we thank you for the leaders who spoke your word to us. Give rest to Bishop Geevarghese Mar Divannasios, strengthen our shepherds as you freed Peter from his chains, and make us faithful stewards found at work when you come. Amen.
altar: Hebrews says “we have an altar” (13:10). At the Qurbono we offer the sacrifice of praise with the leaders who taught us, living and departed.

2027-01-18.title: Monday after the Second Sunday after Denho · First Day of the Fast of the Ninevites
readings: Jonah flees from the presence of the Lord
He humbled himself and became obedient
2027-01-18.alt: Season of Denho. Moonnu Nombu, the fast of the Ninevites (Baooutho d'Ninwoye). Commemoration of Moran Mor Cyril Baselios Catholicos (+2007), first Major Archbishop-Catholicos, and of Joseph Mar Severios: Hebrews 13:7–16; Matthew 24:45–51. Church Unity Octave begins.
2027-01-18.verse: For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.
theo: The fast of the Ninevites begins with a prophet running away. God sends Jonah to Nineveh, “But Jonah set out to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD.” A storm rises; the pagan sailors pray while the prophet sleeps below deck. Jonah is like many of us: we know God's will and go the other way. The Three Days' Fast is our chance to stop running, to turn the ship around.

Paul shows the opposite of Jonah: Christ, “though he was in the form of God”, did not run from the Father's will but “humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross.” In the Gospel Jesus names Jonah as his sign: three days in the sea monster, three days in the tomb, and then the rising. Today we also remember Moran Mor Cyril Baselios, who led our Church as its first Major Archbishop, and Joseph Mar Severios. Hebrews tells us: “Remember your leaders… consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.”
outline: Ask: have you ever known what God wanted and gone the other way?
The prophet asleep in the storm.
“Let the same mind be in you that was in Christ Jesus.”
live: Stop running
Name one thing God is asking of you that you have been avoiding, and begin it today.
Keep the fast
Fast as your health allows and give the saving to the poor.
2027-01-18.prayer: Lord Jesus, you obeyed the Father to the cross and rose on the third day, the true sign of Jonah. As we begin the fast of the Ninevites, turn us back from our flight, humble our hearts, and through the prayers of Moran Mor Cyril Baselios and Joseph Mar Severios keep our Church faithful. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbono makes present the One who went down into death and rose: the sign of Jonah given to us at the altar.

2027-01-19.title: Tuesday after the Second Sunday after Denho · Second Day of the Fast of the Ninevites · Mar Macarios
2027-01-19.alt: Season of Denho. Moonnu Nombu, the fast of the Ninevites (Baooutho d'Ninwoye). Commemoration of Mar Macarios of Jerusalem. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-19.verse: Keep awake therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
theo: On the second day, Jonah finally obeys. He walks a day's journey into the great city and cries his short message. “And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.” The king's decree is remarkable: “All shall turn from their evil ways and from the violence that is in their hands. Who knows? God may relent.” Fasting without turning from violence and evil would mean nothing. Nineveh fasted with its hands as well as its stomach.

Jesus warns that his coming will be like the days of Noah: people “were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage” and did not notice until the flood came. “Keep awake therefore.” Paul tells us how the watchful live: “Let love be genuine; hate what is evil, hold fast to what is good… Rejoice in hope, be patient in suffering, persevere in prayer.” Today we remember Mar Macarios, bishop of Jerusalem in the age of Nicaea, who guarded the true faith and the holy places of the Lord.
outline: Ask: what would you change if you knew Christ would come tonight?
live: Clean hands (Jonah 3:8)
Put right one injustice or harsh word today.
Persevere in prayer (Romans 12:12)
Pray the evening prayer of the Church with your family.
2027-01-19.prayer: Lord God, the people of Nineveh believed you and turned from violence and evil. Keep us awake for the coming of your Son, make our love genuine, and through the prayers of Mar Macarios keep us steadfast in the true faith. Amen.
altar: Every Holy Qurbono looks forward to the coming of the Lord: we keep awake at the altar, awaiting him who comes.

2027-01-20.title: Wednesday after the Second Sunday after Denho · Third Day of the Fast of the Ninevites · St Sebastian
readings: Jonah's prayer from the belly of the fish
2027-01-20.alt: Season of Denho. Moonnu Nombu, the fast of the Ninevites (Baooutho d'Ninwoye). St Sebastian, martyr. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-20.verse: saying, “I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me; out of the belly of Sheol I cried, and you heard my voice.
theo: On the third day we hear Jonah praying from the depths. Swallowed by the great fish, at the bottom of the sea, with weeds wrapped around his head, he does not despair: “I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me.” “As my life was ebbing away, I remembered the LORD; and my prayer came to you.” And on the third day the fish spews him onto dry land. The Fathers saw here Christ's descent into death and his rising, and also our Baptism: going down into the water and coming up to new life.

In the Gospel people tell Jesus of a disaster in Jerusalem, and he answers: do not think the victims were worse sinners than you; “unless you repent, you will all perish as they did.” Repentance is not for others; it is for me, now. Paul says: “you are all children of light and children of the day”; let us “keep awake and be sober.” Today the Church honours St Sebastian, the soldier who served Christ more than Caesar and twice faced death for him. Jonah prayed in the depths; Sebastian stood firm under the arrows. Both teach us that no depth is beyond God's hearing.
outline: Ask: when did you feel you were at the bottom of the sea?
“I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me.”
live: Pray from your depths (Jonah 2:2)
Tell God honestly about your deepest trouble.
Confess before the fast ends
Make your confession today or tomorrow.
2027-01-20.prayer: Lord our God, you heard Jonah from the belly of the fish and brought him up on the third day. Hear us in our distress, give us true repentance, and through the prayers of St Sebastian make us brave children of the light. Amen.
altar: Christ went down into the depths of death and rose; in the Holy Qurbono he lifts us up with him.

2027-01-21.title: Thursday after the Second Sunday after Denho · Conclusion of the Fast of the Ninevites · St Agnes
readings: Abraham pleads for Sodom; Joshua's prayer
Should I not be concerned about Nineveh?
God revealed his Son to me
Something greater than Jonah is here
2027-01-21.alt: Season of Denho. Conclusion of Moonnu Nombu. St Agnes, virgin and martyr. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-21.verse: For just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will be to this generation.
theo: The fast ends with a surprise: the prophet is angry that God was merciful. Nineveh has repented and been spared, and Jonah sulks under a bush. God asks him: “Is it right for you to be angry?” and ends the book with a question that is addressed to us: “should I not be concerned about Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons who do not know their right hand from their left, and also many animals?” The fast is complete only when our heart becomes as wide as God's mercy, even for those we dislike.

Abraham pleads for Sodom: “Suppose ten are found there.” Joshua falls on his face before the ark. Saul, the persecutor, is thrown down on the road and called; he later writes that God “was pleased to reveal his Son to me, so that I might proclaim him among the Gentiles.” And Jesus says: “something greater than Jonah is here!” The Ninevites believed a reluctant prophet; we have the Son of God himself. Today we also remember St Agnes, the young Roman girl who gave her life for Christ. She shows that the response to Christ can be total even in the young.
outline: Ask: have you ever been upset that someone you disliked was forgiven?
A narrow heart before a wide mercy.
Christ, the sign; Paul, the converted.
live: Widen your heart (Jonah 4:11)
Pray today for someone you find hard to forgive.
Intercede like Abraham (Genesis 18:32)
Pray for your town or city by name.
2027-01-21.prayer: Merciful God, you spared Nineveh and rebuked the narrow heart of your prophet. As the fast ends, make our hearts as wide as your mercy, teach us to intercede like Abraham, and through the prayers of St Agnes give us her undivided love for Christ, who is greater than Jonah. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the One greater than Jonah is present: not a sign only, but the Lord himself.

2027-01-22.title: Friday after the Second Sunday after Denho · Mar Timotheos the Apostle
readings: Fight the good fight of the faith
Not to abolish but to fulfil
2027-01-22.alt: Season of Denho. Commemoration of Mar Timotheos, disciple of St Paul. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-22.verse: Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of the eternal life, to which you were called and for which you made the good confession in the presence of many witnesses.
theo: Today our Church remembers Mar Timotheos, the young disciple whom Paul called “my loyal child in the faith”. Paul's charge to him is a programme for every Christian: “pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, gentleness. Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of the eternal life, to which you were called.” Timothy was timid, often unwell and young for his office, yet he became a shepherd of the church in Ephesus. God's strength is shown in such weakness.

In the Gospel Jesus says: “Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.” The Christian faith does not throw away the Old Testament; it reads it in the light of Christ, as our liturgy does every day. Timothy learned the Scriptures from childhood at the knees of his mother and grandmother, and Paul taught him to see Christ in them. Our families too can be the first school of the word.
outline: Ask: who first taught you the faith?
Christ completes the law and prophets.
“Fight the good fight of the faith.”
live: Pursue one virtue (1 Timothy 6:11)
Choose one of the six virtues Paul lists and practise it today.
Teach the faith at home
Read a Bible story with a child this week.
2027-01-22.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came not to abolish but to fulfil. Through the prayers of Mar Timotheos make us fight the good fight of the faith, take hold of eternal life, and hand on the faith in our homes as Lois and Eunice did. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the Old Testament and the Gospel are read together: Christ fulfils all, and then gives himself to us.

2027-01-23.title: Saturday after the Second Sunday after Denho
readings: The mediator of a better covenant
2027-01-23.alt: Season of Denho. Church Unity Octave. Tomorrow is Kohne Sunday, the commemoration of departed priests.
2027-01-23.verse: But Jesus has now obtained a more excellent ministry, and to that degree he is the mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted through better promises.
theo: Hebrews gives us “the main point”: “we have such a high priest, one who is seated at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens”. The priests of the old covenant served “a sketch and shadow of the heavenly one”; Jesus serves in the true sanctuary and is “the mediator of a better covenant”. Tomorrow is Kohne Sunday, when our Church prays for its departed priests. Every priest, living or departed, shares in the one priesthood of Christ, and is a weak vessel of his grace.

In the Gospel a mute man, possessed by a demon, is brought to Jesus. When the demon is cast out, “the one who had been mute spoke; and the crowds were amazed.” Christ opens mouths to praise God. Yet the Pharisees say he works by the ruler of demons. The same act brings wonder to some and suspicion to others. Let our mouths, opened by Christ in Baptism, be used for praise and witness, and let us pray tomorrow for the priests who taught us to speak the faith.
outline: Ask: which priest has most helped you in your faith?
Christ opens our mouths for praise.
live: Prepare for Kohne Sunday
Write down the names of departed priests you knew, to pray for them tomorrow.
Open your lips (Psalm 51:15)
Speak one word of faith or praise to someone today.
2027-01-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, our great high priest, mediator of a better covenant, open our lips to praise you. Bless all priests who serve your Church, and grant rest to the priests who have gone before us in faith. Amen.
altar: At the altar the priest stands in the person of Christ, the one high priest, who offers himself in the Holy Qurbono for us.

2027-01-25.title: Monday after Kohne Sunday · Conversion of St Paul
readings: The call of Saul on the road to Damascus
He proclaims the faith he once tried to destroy
That they may all be one
2027-01-25.alt: Season of Denho. Anniversary of the erection of the eparchies of Pathanamthitta and Puttur (2010). Church Unity Octave concludes.
2027-01-25.verse: that they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
theo: Our Church keeps the Conversion of Paul with the prayer of Jesus for unity. Saul, “still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord”, is thrown down by a light from heaven and hears: “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” Blind for three days, he waits in Damascus, neither eating nor drinking. Paul later tells the Galatians the whole story without hiding his past: “I was violently persecuting the church of God and was trying to destroy it.” Then the churches of Judea “only heard it said, ‘The one who formerly was persecuting us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy.’ And they glorified God because of me.”

The Gospel is from the prayer of Jesus the night before he died: “that they may all be one… so that the world may believe that you have sent me.” Division among Christians hides Christ from the world; unity reveals him. Paul, who once tore the Church apart, became the great builder of its unity. Our own Church was born of a longing for that unity when, in 1930, Mar Ivanios and his companions entered into communion with the See of Rome. Today we also give thanks for the eparchies of Pathanamthitta and Puttur, erected in 2010, and pray that our Church may always be a bridge of communion.
outline: Ask: can the worst enemy of the Church become its greatest apostle?
Breathing threats, then blind and waiting.
Grace that turns a life around.
Point 3 · That they may all be one
“That they may all be one… so that the world may believe.”
live: Pray for unity (John 17:21)
Pray today for Christians of another Church by name.
Do not despair of anyone (Galatians 1:23)
Pray for someone who is hostile to the faith.
2027-01-25.prayer: Lord Jesus, you turned Saul the persecutor into Paul the apostle. Make all your disciples one, as you and the Father are one, so that the world may believe. Bless the eparchies of Pathanamthitta and Puttur, and keep our Church a bridge of communion. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono we pray for the unity of the Church and receive the one Body that makes us one.

2027-01-26.title: Tuesday after Kohne Sunday · Republic Day of India
readings: You are a letter of Christ
Give to the emperor what is the emperor's, and to God what is God's
2027-01-26.alt: Season of Denho. Republic Day of India.
2027-01-26.verse: They answered, “The emperor's.” Then he said to them, “Give therefore to the emperor the things that are the emperor's, and to God the things that are God's.”
theo: Some in Corinth wanted letters of recommendation from Paul. He answers: “You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, to be known and read by all; and you show that you are a letter of Christ… written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.” The best proof of the Gospel is a changed community. And Paul is humble: “Not that we are competent of ourselves… our competence is from God.”

On Republic Day the Gospel could not be more fitting. The Pharisees and Herodians try to trap Jesus: is it lawful to pay taxes to the emperor? He asks for a coin: “Whose head is this, and whose title?” “The emperor's.” “Give therefore to the emperor the things that are the emperor's, and to God the things that are God's.” The coin bears Caesar's image; we bear God's image. Christians are loyal citizens: we pay taxes, obey just laws, vote, serve the common good and pray for those in authority. But the State is not God. Our deepest belonging is to God, and that gives us the courage to stand for justice, for the poor, and for the freedom of conscience that India's Constitution guarantees to all.
outline: Ask: whose image is on a rupee note? Whose image is on you?
“Give… to God the things that are God's.”
live: Be a good citizen
Pay what you owe honestly and obey just laws; vote with a formed conscience.
Give God what is his
Offer God your whole self in prayer today.
2027-01-26.prayer: Lord God, you made us in your image and wrote your Spirit on our hearts. On this Republic Day bless India and its people of every faith; grant wisdom and justice to those who govern; and make us loyal citizens who give to God the things that are God's. Amen.
altar: At the Qurbono we pray for the nation and its rulers, as the Church has always done, and offer ourselves wholly to God.

2027-01-27.title: Wednesday after Kohne Sunday
readings: Christ and the Church: a great mystery
Marriage is not to be broken
2027-01-27.verse: Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her,
theo: Paul begins with a principle for every Christian household: “Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ.” Mutual self-giving, not domination, is the law of Christian marriage. He then speaks to wives and husbands in the language of his time, but turns everything toward Christ: “Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her.” The measure of a husband's love is the cross. Quoting Genesis, “the two will become one flesh”, Paul adds: “This is a great mystery, and I am applying it to Christ and the church.”

In the Gospel Jesus restores marriage to God's original plan. Moses had allowed a certificate of divorce, but Jesus teaches that the bond is not to be broken. The Church calls marriage a sacrament, a living icon of Christ's faithful love for his Bride; in our tradition the Crowning shows husband and wife as king and queen of a small kingdom, the domestic church. Today let us pray for married couples, for families under strain, and for those whose marriages have been wounded, that they may find in the Church the mercy and truth of Christ.
outline: Ask: what makes love last a lifetime?
Point 2 · As Christ loved the Church
Point 3 · One flesh, a great mystery
“Just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her.”
live: Serve your spouse (Ephesians 5:21)
Do one act of humble service for your husband or wife today.
Pray for families
Pray for a couple you know who are struggling.
2027-01-27.prayer: Lord Jesus, you love the Church as a faithful Bridegroom and gave yourself up for her. Bless all married couples with mutual reverence, faithful love and the grace to forgive. Heal wounded families, and make every home a domestic church. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbono is the wedding feast of the Lamb; the self-giving of Christ on the altar is the model of every marriage.

2027-01-28.title: Thursday after Kohne Sunday · St Thomas Aquinas
readings: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever
I am the way, and the truth, and the life
2027-01-28.alt: Season of Denho. Alternative Gospel: Matthew 24:45–51. Commemoration of Fr John Kuzhinapurath. St Thomas Aquinas, Doctor of the Church.
2027-01-28.verse: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
theo: Hebrews gives a community in change three anchors. Remember your leaders who spoke God's word to you, and imitate their faith. Hold to Christ, who does not change: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.” And worship in two ways: “let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name. Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.” Praise and charity are the Christian's sacrifices.

In the Gospel Jesus comforts his troubled disciples: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me. In my Father's house there are many dwelling places.” Thomas asks: “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?” And Jesus answers with one of the greatest sentences of the Gospel: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.” In this week of Kohne we remember the priests who showed us that way, among them Fr John Kuzhinapurath, and St Thomas Aquinas, who gave his mind to the Truth and his heart to the Life.
outline: Ask: who first showed you the way to God?
Point 3 · The way, the truth, the life
“I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”
live: Remember your priests (Hebrews 13:7)
Pray for a priest, living or departed, who helped your faith.
Sacrifice of sharing (Hebrews 13:16)
Share something you have with someone in need.
2027-01-28.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, the same yesterday and today and forever, you are the way, the truth and the life. Grant eternal rest to Fr John Kuzhinapurath and all our departed priests; through the prayers of St Thomas Aquinas give us minds that seek truth and hearts that offer praise and charity. Amen.
altar: Through Christ the priest we offer the sacrifice of praise; at the altar he who is the Way leads us to the Father.

2027-01-29.title: Friday after Kohne Sunday · Mar Ignatius Noorono of Antioch
readings: Present your bodies as a living sacrifice
Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies
2027-01-29.alt: Season of Denho. Commemoration of Mar Ignatius Noorono (the fiery), bishop of Antioch and martyr; name day of Joshua Mar Ignathios.
2027-01-29.verse: Very truly, I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
theo: Some Greeks come to Philip with a simple request: “Sir, we wish to see Jesus.” Jesus answers by speaking of his death: “unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.” To see Jesus truly is to see the cross.
