And the disciple follows the same path: “Whoever serves me must follow me, and where I am, there will my servant be also.” Paul applies this to daily life: “present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God… Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your minds.”

Our Church today honours Mar Ignatius of Antioch, called Noorono, the fiery one, the third bishop of Antioch after St Peter. Condemned to the beasts in Rome around the year 107, he wrote seven letters on the journey, urging unity with the bishop and love of the Eucharist, and saying that he wished to be God's wheat, ground by the teeth of beasts, so as to become the pure bread of Christ. He lived the Gospel of the grain of wheat. We also pray for Joshua Mar Ignathios on his name day, and for all who serve the Body of Christ with their gifts, as Paul says: “we, who are many, are one body in Christ.”
outline: Ask: what happens to a seed that refuses to be planted?
Point 1 · We wish to see Jesus
“If it dies, it bears much fruit.”
live: Offer your body (Romans 12:1)
Offer today's work and tiredness to God as a living sacrifice.
Use your gift (Romans 12:6)
Use one gift you have for the parish or for someone in need.
2027-01-29.prayer: Lord Jesus, grain of wheat who fell into the earth and rose to bear much fruit, make us a living sacrifice. Through the prayers of Mar Ignatius Noorono, kindle in us his fiery love for you and for your Church; bless Joshua Mar Ignathios on his name day. Amen.
altar: Mar Ignatius called the Eucharist the medicine of immortality. In the Qurbono the Grain of wheat becomes our Bread.

2027-01-30.title: Saturday after Kohne Sunday · Mar Jacob Aphrahat, the Persian Sage
readings: The tree is known by its fruit
2027-01-30.alt: Season of Denho. Commemoration of Mar Jacob Aphrahat, the Persian Sage; Sts Hyacintha and Martina.
2027-01-30.verse: The good person brings good things out of a good treasure, and the evil person brings evil things out of an evil treasure.
theo: Paul asks the Corinthians, who were busy testing him, to turn the test around: “Examine yourselves to see whether you are living in the faith. Test yourselves. Do you not realize that Jesus Christ is in you?” And he states a principle for every Christian: “we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.” Saturday, before the Lord's Day, is a good time for an examination of conscience.

In the Gospel Jesus says: “the tree is known by its fruit.” What we say reveals what we are: “out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.” And he warns: “on the day of judgment you will have to give an account for every careless word you utter.” Today the Syriac tradition remembers Mar Jacob Aphrahat, the Persian Sage of the fourth century, the earliest Syriac Father whose writings survive. In his Demonstrations he spoke of faith as a house built on the rock of Christ, and taught that the heart is the true temple where Christ dwells. We remember too Sts Hyacintha and Martina. Let us examine our hearts, so that our words may come from a good treasure.
outline: Ask: what do your words this week say about your heart?
Point 2 · The tree and its fruit
Aphrahat and the temple of the heart.
“Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.”
live: Examine (2 Corinthians 13:5)
Make an examination of conscience tonight, especially on your words.
Guard your mouth (Psalm 141:3)
Avoid one careless or hurtful word today.
2027-01-30.prayer: Lord Jesus, you dwell in our hearts. Search us and know us; make the tree good so that its fruit may be good. Through the prayers of Mar Jacob Aphrahat and Sts Hyacintha and Martina, fill our hearts with good treasure and our mouths with words of truth and kindness. Amen.
altar: We prepare for the Lord's Day by examining our hearts, so that we may approach the altar with clean lips.

quick: Jesus means “the Lord saves”.
Begin the year with a Name, not just a wish.
Put off the old self and put on the new.
2027-01-01.action: Name one old habit to leave behind and one virtue to put on this year.
2027-01-01.question: Under whose name will I live this year?
2027-01-01.special: The Naming of our Lord and New Year's Day. World Day of Peace.
illus: An illustration

In many Kerala homes the first thing written in a new notebook or account book is a cross, or “Jesus” at the top of the first page. It is a small act of faith: everything that follows is placed under his Name.

family.explain: When Jesus was eight days old, Mary and Joseph gave him the name the angel had told them: Jesus, which means “God saves”.
family.intention: We offer this new year to Jesus and pray for peace in our family and in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing will each of us try to do this year?”

catechism: Prayer in the name of Jesus.
kidsaint: A bishop in Caesarea who built a whole “new city” for the poor and sick, with hospitals and kitchens. Lesson: begin the new year by helping someone in need.
term: Jesus (Yeshua) means “the Lord saves”. Christians pray in this Name, bow at it, and begin their work under it. The ancient Jesus Prayer is: “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.”
termMore: Jewish boys were circumcised and named on the eighth day (Leviticus 12:3). The feast falls on 1 January, the octave day of Yaldo, which is also the civil New Year.

quick: The Child of Bethlehem is the Lamb of God.
Conversion bears fruit: share your second coat.
Those who wait for the Lord renew their strength.
2027-01-03.action: Give away one good item of clothing or food this week.
2027-01-03.question: What is my “second coat” that someone else needs?
2027-01-03.special: Second Sunday after Yaldo. Announce Denho on Wednesday 6 January, a day of obligation.
illus: An illustration

After Christmas many Kerala homes have cupboards full of new clothes. One parish asks families to bring one good garment to church on the Sunday after Christmas for the poor. The pile at the door is John the Baptist's sermon in action.

family.explain: John the Baptist said: if you have two shirts, give one away. And he pointed to Jesus and said: “Look, the Lamb of God!”
family.intention: We pray for people who are cold or hungry this January.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share this week?”

kidsaint: A priest from Kainakary in Kerala who started schools beside churches so that every child could learn, founded religious congregations and printed books. Lesson: learning is a gift from God; use it to help others.
term: John the Baptist's name for Jesus (John 1:29). It recalls the Passover lamb and the Suffering Servant of Isaiah: Jesus gives his life to take away the sin of the world.
termMore: The days from Christmas to the Baptism of the Lord unfold one mystery: God revealed in Christ, to the shepherds, to the Magi, and at the Jordan.

quick: Denho: at the Jordan the Holy Trinity is revealed.
Christ, who has no sin, sanctifies the waters for our Baptism.
In Baptism the Father calls each of us “my beloved child”.
2027-01-06.action: Find out the date of your Baptism and thank God for it today.
2027-01-06.question: Do I live as the Father's beloved child?
2027-01-06.special: Denho, the Baptism of our Lord: day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people.
illus: An illustration

In old Kerala Christian homes the date of Baptism was written inside the family Bible, beside the date of birth. Many grandparents knew it better than their birthday. Denho reminds us that the second birth matters even more than the first.

family.explain: Jesus was baptised by John in the river Jordan. Heaven opened, the Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and the Father said: “This is my beloved Son.” At our Baptism God said the same about us!
family.intention: We thank God for our Baptism and pray for our godparents.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we know the day each of us was baptised, and who our godparents are?”

kidsaint: He lived in the desert, called people to change their hearts, and had the joy of baptising Jesus. He said: “He must increase, but I must decrease.” Lesson: point others to Jesus, not to yourself.
term: Syriac for “rising” or “dawn”: the manifestation of Christ at his Baptism in the Jordan, 6 January. In the Malankara tradition the waters are solemnly blessed on this feast, and the faithful take the blessed water home.
termMore: From the early centuries the Eastern Churches celebrated on 6 January the manifestation of Christ, above all his Baptism. The season of Denho continues until the Great Fast.

quick: Jesus begins his mission by calling people.
God calls in the middle of ordinary work.
Leave the nets: following Christ needs a real decision.
2027-01-10.action: Invite one person to Holy Qurbono or a prayer meeting this week.
2027-01-10.question: What nets do I need to leave to follow Jesus more closely?
illus: An illustration

Many priests and sisters from Kerala's coastal parishes grew up in fishing families. More than one says the call came while helping father mend the nets. The Gospel of the lake keeps happening in Kerala.

family.explain: Jesus walked by the lake and saw fishermen. He said: “Follow me!” They left their nets at once and went with him.
family.intention: We pray for vocations to the priesthood and religious life from our family and parish.
family.ask: Ask: “What is Jesus asking our family to do for him?”

catechism: Jesus calls disciples into communion with him.
Every person is called to love and serve.
kidsaint: Simon was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee. When Jesus called him, he left his boat and nets and followed him. Jesus made him the leader of the apostles. Lesson: say yes quickly when Jesus calls.
term: The season after the Baptism of the Lord, until the Great Fast. Its Sundays show Christ revealed in his ministry: calling disciples, teaching, and showing his glory.
termMore: At the burning bush Moses removed his sandals (Exodus 3:5). In many Eastern churches the faithful still remove their sandals before entering the sanctuary area.

quick: “Come and see”: the best way to bring someone to Christ.
Christ is the ladder between heaven and earth.
The Nineveh fast begins tomorrow: return to God.
2027-01-17.action: Invite one person to “come and see” this week.
2027-01-17.question: Whom can I invite to come and see Jesus?
2027-01-17.special: Second Sunday after Denho. Remind the faithful: the Nineveh fast (three days) is from Monday 18 to Wednesday 20 January, with the special prayers and abstinence.
illus: An illustration

A young engineer in the Gulf stopped going to church for years. A colleague never argued with him, but every Friday said, “Come with me to Qurbono, just once.” One day he came, and he still goes. “Come and see” is still how faith spreads.

family.explain: Philip told Nathanael about Jesus. Nathanael was not sure, so Philip said: “Come and see!” When Nathanael met Jesus, he believed.
family.intention: We pray for friends and relatives who have drifted away from the Church.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we keep the Nineveh fast together as a family?”

catechism: Many forms of penance; the Nineveh fast.
kidsaint: A young man who heard the Gospel “sell what you own and give to the poor” and did it. He went to pray in the desert, and many came to learn from him. Lesson: when you hear God's Word, do it.
term: Three days of fasting before the Great Fast, recalling the repentance of Nineveh at Jonah's preaching (Jonah 3). The Malankara lectionary asks for special prayers, prostrations and abstinence in these days.
termMore: Jesus himself said “Come and see” to his first disciples (John 1:39); Philip repeats it to Nathanael. Faith passes from friend to friend.

quick: Kohne Sunday: we remember the departed priests.
The priesthood continues: Christ is the one High Priest.
“Remember your leaders and imitate their faith.”
2027-01-24.action: Pray by name for the priests who served your family.
2027-01-24.question: Which priest helped my faith most, and how can I thank God for him?
2027-01-24.special: Kohne Sunday, commemoration of the departed priests. (In 2025–26 also Catholicos Day; check the 2026–27 lectionary for collections.)
illus: An illustration

In many Kerala parishes the tombs of former vicars lie near the church door. On Kohne Sunday the people light candles there after Qurbono. Some of those priests baptised the grandparents of today's children.

family.explain: Priests bring us Jesus in the Holy Qurbono and in Confession. Today we thank God for priests who have died and pray that they are happy with Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for the priests who have died, for our parish priest, and for new vocations.
family.ask: Ask: “Which priest baptised each of us? Let us pray for him.”

catechism: Purification after death and prayer for the dead.
kidsaint: A priest in Turin who gathered poor boys from the streets, taught them a trade, played with them and led them to Jesus. Lesson: priests are fathers who care for us; pray for them.
term: Kohne is Syriac for “priests”. The first of three Sundays of remembrance before the Great Fast: departed priests (Kohne), all the departed faithful (Aneede), then the Fast begins with Kothine (Cana) Sunday.
termMore: Before entering the Great Fast, the Church remembers her dead: it is a reminder that Lent is a journey towards Easter, the victory over death.

quick: Aneede Sunday: we remember all the faithful departed.
Christian grief has hope: we will be with the Lord for ever.
We will be judged on love: what we did for the least.
2027-01-31.action: Offer a Qurbono and pray daily this week for your departed family members.
2027-01-31.question: How am I preparing for my own meeting with the Lord?
2027-01-31.special: Aneede Sunday, commemoration of the faithful departed. Announce the beginning of the Great Fast with Kothine Sunday (7 February) and the Shubkono on Monday 8 February.
illus: An illustration

In Kerala families the name of a departed parent is written in the parish register for the annual Qurbono, and the family gathers every year on that day. Love does not stop at the grave; it becomes prayer.

family.explain: When people we love die, we are sad. But Jesus rose from the dead, and he will raise them too. We pray for them so that they may be happy with God.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and all our family members who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family has gone to God? Let us tell one good memory of them.”

kidsaint: The mother of St Augustine, who prayed for her son for many years until he came back to God. Before she died she asked him only to remember her at the altar. Lesson: pray for those you love, living and dead.
term: Aneede is Syriac for “the departed”. On the Sunday before the Great Fast the Malankara Church remembers all the faithful departed, after remembering the departed priests on Kohne Sunday.
termMore: Why do we pray for the dead?
Because love does not end with death, and because the dead who still need purification can be helped by the prayers and offerings of the living (2 Maccabees 12:45; CCC 1032).

quick: Basil and Gregory defended the Trinity and were gentle shepherds.
We must be born of water and Spirit.
The Son of Man is lifted up to give eternal life.
2027-01-02.action: Pray today for our Catholicos and bishops.
2027-01-02.question: Do I live as one born from above?

family.explain: A teacher named Nicodemus came to Jesus at night. Jesus told him: you must be born again, from water and the Holy Spirit. That happens in Baptism!
family.intention: We pray for our Catholicos and bishops.
family.ask: Ask: “Where were you baptised? Who are your godparents?”

illus: An illustration

A retired headmaster in Mavelikara was known for one habit: he never corrected a student in front of others. He would call the boy aside, speak quietly, and end with a blessing. Decades later his old students said they remembered his gentleness more than his lessons.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you told Nicodemus that we must be born from above. Renew in us the grace of our Baptism as we gather. Amen.
share: No one can enter the kingdom without being born of water and Spirit (John 3:5). How do I live my Baptism?
The Son of Man must be lifted up (John 3:14). What does the Cross mean to me?
The Lord's servant must be kindly to everyone (2 Timothy 2:24). How can I correct others with gentleness?
pm.resp: Lord, renew us by your Spirit.
interc: For our Catholicos, Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis, on his name day.
For the Eparchy of Mavelikara and all our eparchies.
For teachers and catechists, that they may be gentle and patient.
For those seeking God by night, like Nicodemus.
For our group, that we may live as people born from above.
pm.close: Father, through water and the Spirit you gave us new birth. Through the prayers of Mar Baselios and Mar Gregorios, keep us faithful to the faith of the Church and gentle with all. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Without faith it is impossible to please God.
The Beatitudes show the face of a life of faith.
Malachi and St Chavara point to the Sun of righteousness.
2027-01-04.action: Choose one Beatitude and live it deliberately this week.
2027-01-04.question: Which Beatitude is hardest for me?

family.explain: Jesus taught on a mountain: blessed are the gentle, the merciful, the peacemakers. God makes them truly happy.
family.intention: We pray that our family may be peacemakers.
family.ask: Ask: “Which of these blessings would you like to live this week?”

illus: An illustration

When St Chavara saw that poor children in Kerala had no schools, he did not write complaints; he opened schools beside churches and even arranged midday meals so that poor children would come. Meekness and hunger for righteousness became a school bell.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you went up the mountain and taught the Beatitudes. Teach us now, and give us pure hearts. Amen.
share: Without faith it is impossible to please God (Hebrews 11:6). How do I show my faith in deeds?
Blessed are the pure in heart (Matthew 5:8). What clouds my heart?
St Chavara lived the Beatitudes in Kerala. Which saint of our land inspires me?
pm.resp: Lord, make us blessed in your ways.
interc: For the Church in Kerala, that she may be rich in saints.
For teachers and schools, through St Chavara.
For the poor in spirit and those who mourn.
For peacemakers in our families and society.
For our group, that we may prepare well for Denho.
pm.close: Father, you raised up prophets and saints to prepare the way of your Son. Give us faith that pleases you and hearts pure enough to see you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Christ gives gifts to build up his Body.
We grow into Christ by speaking the truth in love.
Do not worry: the Father clothes the lilies.
2027-01-05.action: Entrust your biggest worry to God in prayer tonight.
2027-01-05.question: What worry keeps me from trusting God?

family.explain: Jesus said: look at the birds and the flowers. God feeds the birds and makes the flowers beautiful. He will take care of you too!
family.intention: We pray for our relatives working and studying in other countries.
family.ask: Ask: “What are you worried about? Let us give it to God together.”

illus: An illustration

A Malankara family in Texas faced a job loss two months before their daughter's college fees were due. The mother pinned a small card on the fridge: Consider the lilies. The parish prayer group prayed with them weekly. A new job came, not quickly, but in time. The card is still on the fridge.

pm.open: Heavenly Father, you clothe the lilies and feed the birds. Take our worries as we gather, and help us to grow in Christ. Amen.
share: He gave gifts to build up the body of Christ (Ephesians 4:11–12). What is my gift for the Church?
Speaking the truth in love (Ephesians 4:15). Where do I need to speak the truth with love?
Consider the lilies (Luke 12:27). What worry can I give to God tonight?
interc: For our Church in the USA, Canada and every land of migration.
For pastors and teachers, that they may build up the body of Christ.
For those worried about jobs, debts or health.
For families separated by distance.
For our group, that we may prepare our hearts for Denho.
pm.close: Father, you know what we need before we ask. Free us from worry, build us up as one body in Christ, and prepare us to hear your voice at the Jordan tomorrow. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: John was no reed shaken by the wind.
He is more than a prophet, the messenger before the Lord.
The least in the Kingdom is greater than he, by grace.
2027-01-07.action: Refuse one compromise with the truth today.
2027-01-07.question: Am I firm in faith, or a reed shaken by every wind?

family.explain: Jesus said: John the Baptist is very great. He was strong like a tree, not weak like grass in the wind. He got everyone ready for Jesus.
family.intention: We pray that we may be strong in our faith.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be strong for Jesus at school or at work?”

illus: An illustration
A coconut palm on a Kerala beach bends in every storm but its roots go deep, and it does not fall. A reed by the canal is flattened by the first gust. John the Baptist was a palm rooted in God.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you praised John the Baptist as more than a prophet. Make us firm like him, and grateful for the grace of your Kingdom. Amen.
share: A reed shaken by the wind? (Luke 7:24). What winds shake my faith?
More than a prophet (Luke 7:26). Who prepared the way of Jesus in my life?
The least in the kingdom is greater than he (Luke 7:28). How do I value the grace of my Baptism?
pm.resp: Lord, make us firm in faith.
interc: For the Church, that she may prepare the way of the Lord in our time.
For prophets and preachers, that they may be firm and simple.
For those shaken by doubt or fear.
For those preparing for Baptism.
For our group, that we may walk the way John prepared.
pm.close: Father, you sent John to prepare the way of your Son. Make us firm in faith and grateful for the grace of the Kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Stephen saw the heavens opened and Jesus standing.
He died forgiving his killers, like Jesus.
He began as a servant and ended as a martyr.
2027-01-08.action: Pray by name today for someone who has hurt you.
2027-01-08.question: Whom do I need to forgive as Stephen forgave?

family.explain: Stephen loved Jesus so much that people threw stones at him. But Stephen looked up and saw Jesus in heaven. He prayed: Lord, forgive them!
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we need to forgive? Let us pray for them.”

illus: An illustration

In 1999 Graham Staines and his two young sons were burnt to death in Odisha. His widow Gladys said soon after: I have forgiven the killers, and I have no bitterness. The nation was stunned. A martyr's family showed Stephen's prayer still alive in India.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you received the spirit of Stephen, your first martyr. Give us his faith, his forgiveness and his love. Amen.
share: He saw the heavens opened (Acts 7:56). Do I look to heaven in my trials?
Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:60). Whom must I forgive?
The household of Stephanas devoted themselves to service (1 Corinthians 16:15). How can my family serve the Church?
interc: For persecuted Christians, especially in India.
For deacons and all who serve in the Church.
For Bishop Philipos Mar Stephanos on his name day.
For those who have hurt us, that they may be converted.
For our group, that we may forgive and serve.
pm.close: Father, your servant Stephen saw your glory and forgave his persecutors. Strengthen us to witness and to forgive, and receive us at the end into your glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Our unfaithfulness does not cancel God's faithfulness.
Human customs must not replace God's commandment.
The washing that matters is of the heart.
2027-01-09.action: Examine one religious habit: is it still prayer from the heart?
2027-01-09.question: Do I honour God only with my lips in some part of my life?

family.explain: Some leaders complained that Jesus' friends did not wash their hands in the right way. Jesus said: God wants your heart to be clean, not only your hands!
family.intention: We pray that our hearts may be clean and loving.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we keep our hearts clean?”

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in Thiruvalla prayed the evening prayers every day for sixty years. One day her grandson asked why she sometimes stopped in the middle. She said: when I notice I am only saying words, I stop and tell God I love him, then I continue. Tradition with a heart.

pm.open: Faithful God, you are true even when we fail. Wash our hearts as we gather. Amen.
share: Will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God? (Romans 3:3). When has God been faithful to me?
This people honors me with their lips (Mark 7:6). Where are my lips and heart apart?
You abandon the commandment of God (Mark 7:8). Which custom of mine needs renewal?
pm.resp: Lord, create in us a clean heart.
interc: For the Church, that her traditions may always lead to the living God.
For those who feel their prayer has become empty.
For leaders, that they may not burden people with human rules.
For those who doubt God's faithfulness.
For our group, that our devotion may come from the heart.
pm.close: Faithful Father, you washed us in Baptism and remain true to your promises. Renew our hearts, so that all we do may honour you in truth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God is the Father of mercies and God of all consolation.
Trials teach us to rely on God who raises the dead.
Christ gives the Spirit without measure.
2027-01-11.action: Call or visit someone who is suffering this week.
2027-01-11.question: How can the comfort I received become comfort for someone else?

family.explain: St Paul says God comforts us when we are sad, so that we can comfort others who are sad.
family.intention: We pray for someone in our family or neighbourhood who is sad.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we comfort this week?”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Kollam who lost her son in an accident later joined a parish group visiting bereaved families. She says: I cannot take away their pain, but I can sit with them as someone who knows. God's comfort reached me so that it could reach them.

pm.open: Father of mercies, God of all consolation, comfort us as we gather, and make us comforters of others. Amen.
share: The God of all consolation (2 Corinthians 1:3). When have I felt God's comfort?
Rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead (2 Corinthians 1:9). Where must I trust more?
He gives the Spirit without measure (John 3:34). How do I make room for the Spirit?
interc: For those in grief and affliction.
For those who comfort others in hospitals and homes.
For bishops and theologians, through Mar Gregorios.
For those facing danger or death.
For our group, that we may grow in God's love.
pm.close: Father, you console us so that we may console others. Fill us with your Spirit and make us bearers of your comfort. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God's glory shines in the face of Jesus Christ.
We proclaim Jesus as Lord, not ourselves.
It is lawful to do good on the sabbath.
2027-01-12.action: Visit a sick or lonely person after Sunday Qurbono.
2027-01-12.question: Does my Sunday include works of mercy?

family.explain: A man had a hand that did not work. Jesus said: stretch out your hand! And it was healed. Jesus said it is always right to do good, even on God's day.
family.intention: We pray for people who cannot use their hands or legs.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing can our family do this Sunday?”

illus: An illustration

St Theodosius, a monk of Palestine in the fifth century, built a great monastery and next to it three houses: one for the sick, one for the elderly, one for the poor and mentally ill. Monks went from the choir to the wards and back. People called it a city of prayer and mercy.

pm.open: God of light, you shine in the face of Jesus. Shine in our hearts as we gather, and send us out to do good. Amen.
share: God has shone in our hearts (2 Corinthians 4:6). Where has Christ's light reached me?
We do not proclaim ourselves (2 Corinthians 4:5). Do I seek my own glory?
Stretch out your hand (Matthew 12:13). Whom can I help this week?
pm.resp: Lord, let your light shine in us.
interc: For preachers, that they may proclaim Christ and not themselves.
For the sick, the elderly and the poor.
For monks and religious who unite prayer and service.
For Bishop Yoohanon Mar Theodosius on his name day.
For our group, that we may do good on the Lord's day.
pm.close: Father, your glory shines in the face of Christ. Let it shine through us in works of mercy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Pray for everyone, including rulers.
Christ is the one mediator; God wants all to be saved.
Do not judge: first remove the log from your own eye.
2027-01-13.action: Before criticising anyone today, name one fault of your own.
2027-01-13.question: Whom do I judge instead of praying for?

family.explain: Jesus told a funny story: a man with a big log in his eye wanted to take a tiny speck out of his friend's eye! Let us fix ourselves before we criticise others.
family.intention: We pray for our country's leaders.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we say something kind instead of something critical today?”

illus: An illustration

A parish council in Pathanamthitta was divided by bitter criticism. The vicar asked each member to pray every day for the person they most disagreed with, by name. After three months the meetings changed. One member said: it is hard to keep judging someone you pray for every morning.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, one mediator, teach us to pray for everyone and to stop judging. Amen.
share: Prayers for everyone (1 Timothy 2:1). Whom do I leave out of my prayers?
God desires everyone to be saved (1 Timothy 2:4). Do I share this desire?
The log in your own eye (Matthew 7:3). What is my log?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us all.
interc: For rulers and all in authority.
For our enemies and those we find hard to love.
For those who judge harshly, and those who are judged.
For all who do not yet know the truth.
For our group, that our prayer may be as wide as God's love.
pm.close: Father, you desire all to be saved. Make our prayer universal and our hearts merciful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: All have sinned; all are offered grace as a gift.
Do not fear those who kill the body.
God counts every hair of your head.
2027-01-14.action: Do not hide your faith in one situation today.
2027-01-14.question: Which fear keeps me from living my faith openly?

family.explain: Jesus said: God does not forget even one little sparrow. He knows how many hairs are on your head! Do not be afraid.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What are we afraid of? Let us trust Jesus together.”

illus: An illustration

St Devasahayam, kept in chains for nearly three years, was led from town to town on a buffalo as a public humiliation. Witnesses said he prayed constantly and greeted visitors with peace. Before he was shot at Aralvaimozhy in 1752, he asked for a few minutes to pray. He did not fear those who kill the body.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you tell us not to fear. Give us the courage of your martyrs as we gather. Amen.
share: All have sinned… justified by his grace as a gift (Romans 3:23–24). Do I live from grace or from my own effort?
Do not fear those who kill the body (Luke 12:4). What fear do I need to give to Jesus?
Even the hairs of your head are all counted (Luke 12:7). How does God's care touch me?
interc: For persecuted Christians, especially in Asia.
For the Church in India, through St Devasahayam.
For monks and nuns, through the Forty Martyrs of Sinai.
For those paralysed by fear.
For our group, that we may witness without fear.
pm.close: Father, your martyrs feared you and nothing else. Make us brave witnesses, trusting in your care. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Those who sow bountifully reap bountifully.
God supplies the seed and gives the growth.
Mary is the good soil where the Word bears fruit.
2027-01-15.action: Give cheerfully to one person in need this week.
2027-01-15.question: Is my heart good soil for God's word?

family.explain: St Paul says: if you plant many seeds, you will get a big harvest. God loves people who give with a happy heart.
family.intention: We pray for farmers who grow our food.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we share happily with someone this week?”

illus: An illustration

In some Malankara parishes farmers still bring a small bag of paddy seed to church in January to be blessed before sowing. One elderly farmer in Kunnamkulam said: I have done this for fifty years. The rain is not in my hands, but the seed is in God's hands and Mother Mary's prayers.

pm.open: Lord of the harvest, through the prayers of the Mother of God, bless our sowing and make us cheerful givers. Amen.
share: The one who sows bountifully will reap bountifully (2 Corinthians 9:6). What am I sowing?
God loves a cheerful giver (2 Corinthians 9:7). Do I give cheerfully?
Mary treasured all these words (Luke 2:19). Do I treasure God's word?
pm.resp: Mother of God, pray for us.
interc: For farmers and agricultural workers.
For a good monsoon and a good harvest.
For the Eparchy of Muvattupuzha.
For the hungry, that they may share in the harvest.
For our group, that we may be good soil for God's word.
pm.close: Father, you give seed to the sower and bread for food. Bless our labour and make us generous, through the prayers of Mary. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Remember your leaders and imitate their faith.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and forever.
Be a faithful steward, found at work when he comes.
2027-01-16.action: Pray today for a priest or teacher who formed your faith.
2027-01-16.question: What has the Lord entrusted to me, and am I faithful in it?

family.explain: Jesus told about a good servant who did his work well even when the master was away. When the master came back, he was happy!
family.intention: We pray for our bishops and priests, living and departed.
family.ask: Ask: “What job has God given each of us at home?”

illus: An illustration

An old sacristan in Thiruvalla rang the church bell at 5.30 every morning for forty years, in rain and power cuts. When asked why he never missed a day, he said: the Lord may come any morning; I want him to find me at the bell rope.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, the same yesterday, today and forever, we thank you for our leaders in faith. Make us faithful stewards. Amen.
share: Remember your leaders… imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). Whose faith do I want to imitate?
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:8). Where do I need his steadiness?
Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work (Matthew 24:46). What is my work for the Lord?
interc: For our bishops and priests, that they may be faithful stewards.
For the repose of Bishop Geevarghese Mar Divannasios and all our departed shepherds.
For Christians in chains for the faith, as Peter was.
For those entrusted with families and work.
For our group, that we may be found faithful.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the same for ever. Keep us faithful to the faith our leaders taught us, until he comes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jonah fled from the presence of the Lord.
Christ humbled himself and obeyed to the cross.
Jesus is the sign of Jonah: three days, then the rising.
2027-01-18.action: Begin today one thing God asks of you that you have avoided.
2027-01-18.question: Where am I fleeing from God's will?

family.explain: God told Jonah to go to Nineveh, but Jonah ran away on a ship. A big storm came. We cannot hide from God!
family.intention: We pray for our bishops and for the souls of Moran Mor Cyril Baselios and Joseph Mar Severios.
family.ask: Ask: “What will each of us give up for the three days?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from Thiruvalla, offered a job abroad, had promised his dying father he would look after his mother. He boarded the plane anyway, and for two years felt, in his words, like Jonah asleep in the storm. During Moonnu Nombu he came home for good. He said: the moment I turned the ship around, the storm in me stopped.

pm.open: Lord, as we begin the fast of the Ninevites, stop our running and turn us back to you. Amen.
share: Jonah set out to flee from the presence of the LORD (Jonah 1:3). Where am I running?
He humbled himself and became obedient (Philippians 2:8). What would obedience look like for me?
The sign of Jonah (Matthew 12:39). Do I believe in the Resurrection with my whole life?
pm.resp: Lord, turn us back to you.
interc: For our Church, as we keep the fast of the Ninevites.
For the soul of Moran Mor Cyril Baselios and of Joseph Mar Severios.
For those running from God's call.
For Christian unity.
For our group, that we may obey as Christ obeyed.
pm.close: Father, your Son humbled himself and rose on the third day. Give us his mind and his obedience. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Nineveh fasted and turned from violence and evil.
Keep awake, for the Lord comes unexpectedly.
Let love be genuine; persevere in prayer.
2027-01-19.action: Put right one injustice or harsh word today.
2027-01-19.question: Is my fasting also a turning from evil?

family.explain: The king of Nineveh told everyone to stop doing bad things and pray. God saw that they changed, and he forgave them.
family.intention: We pray that our homes may be places of peace, without harsh words.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone in our family we need to say sorry to?”

illus: An illustration

A shopkeeper in Mavelikara kept Moonnu Nombu strictly every year. One year his parish priest asked him whether he also paid his workers fairly. That year he raised their wages before the fast began. He said: Nineveh's king did not only fast; he told people to take the violence out of their hands.

pm.open: Lord, keep us awake for your coming, and let our fasting turn us from evil. Amen.
share: All shall turn from their evil ways (Jonah 3:8). What must I turn from?
Keep awake therefore (Matthew 24:42). Am I spiritually asleep?
Let love be genuine (Romans 12:9). Is my love sincere?
interc: For true conversion during the Three Days' Fast.
For an end to violence in our land.
For those spiritually asleep.
For the Church of Jerusalem, through Mar Macarios.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, give us watchful hearts, clean hands and genuine love as we wait for your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jonah prayed from the depths and God heard him.
Unless we repent we will perish.
We are children of light; stay awake and sober.
2027-01-20.action: Make your confession before the fast ends.
2027-01-20.question: Do I think repentance is for others, or for me?

family.explain: Inside the big fish, Jonah prayed to God, and God heard him! After three days the fish put Jonah on the land.
family.intention: We pray for those who feel lost and alone, and for soldiers and police, through St Sebastian.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we need to pray to God for help?”

illus: An illustration

A fisherman from Alappuzha was lost at sea for two nights after his boat capsized, clinging to a plastic can. He says he prayed the words of Jonah he had heard in church during Moonnu Nombu. On the third morning a trawler found him. Each year now he keeps the fast in thanksgiving.

pm.open: Lord, you hear us even from the depths. Give us true repentance on this last day of the fast. Amen.
share: I called to the LORD out of my distress (Jonah 2:2). What distress can I bring to God?
Unless you repent (Luke 13:3). What do I still need to repent of?
You are all children of light (1 Thessalonians 5:5). Where do I live in darkness?
interc: For all who feel trapped in the depths.
For those lost at sea and their families.
For soldiers and police, through St Sebastian.
For true repentance in our Church.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, you heard Jonah from the depths and raised your Son from the grave. Raise us to new life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jonah was angry at God's mercy; God widened his heart.
Abraham and Joshua interceded for others.
Jesus is greater than Jonah.
2027-01-21.action: Pray today for someone you find hard to forgive.
2027-01-21.question: Is my heart as wide as God's mercy?

family.explain: Jonah was cross that God forgave Nineveh. God told him: I love all those people and even their animals! God wants us to love everyone too.
family.intention: We pray for St Agnes's help to love Jesus with our whole heart.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we find hard to love? Let us pray for them.”

illus: An illustration

After a land dispute, two brothers in Pathanamthitta had not spoken for ten years. At the end of Moonnu Nombu the elder heard the last verse of Jonah and could not sleep. The next morning he walked to his brother's house with a packet of sweets. He said: God was concerned about Nineveh; how could I not be concerned about my own brother?

pm.open: Merciful God, as the fast ends, widen our hearts to the measure of your mercy. Amen.
share: Is it right for you to be angry? (Jonah 4:4). Where do I resent God's mercy to others?
Suppose ten are found there (Genesis 18:32). For whom do I intercede?
Something greater than Jonah is here (Luke 11:32). Do I listen to Christ more than Nineveh listened to Jonah?
pm.resp: Lord, make our hearts like yours.
interc: In thanksgiving for the graces of Moonnu Nombu.
For those we find hard to forgive.
For our towns and cities.
For young people, through St Agnes.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, you are concerned for every person you have made. Make us merciful as you are merciful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Fight the good fight of the faith.
Christ fulfils the law and the prophets.
Faith is handed on in families.
2027-01-22.action: Read a Bible story with a child this week.
2027-01-22.question: Am I fighting the good fight, or have I given up?

family.explain: Timothy learned about God from his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice. Our families teach us about God too!
family.intention: We pray in thanksgiving for those who taught us the faith.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught you your first prayer?”

illus: An illustration

A priest from Marthandam remembers that his grandmother could not read, but she knew the Psalms by heart from years of the Church's prayers. Each evening she sang them as she lit the lamp. He says: I learned the Scriptures from her mouth before I learned them from a book, just as Timothy did.

pm.open: Lord, make us faithful disciples like Timothy, fighting the good fight of the faith. Amen.
share: Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, gentleness (1 Timothy 6:11). Which do I most need?
I have come not to abolish but to fulfill (Matthew 5:17). Do I read the Old Testament with Christ in view?
A faith that lived first in your grandmother (2 Timothy 1:5). Whose faith lives in me?
interc: For bishops and priests, through Mar Timotheos.
For young people called to ministry.
For parents and grandparents who teach the faith.
For catechists.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, you gave Timothy as a shepherd to your Church. Make us faithful in the good fight and generous in handing on the faith. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus is our high priest at God's right hand.
He is the mediator of a better covenant.
He opens the mouths of the mute to praise God.
2027-01-23.action: Write the names of departed priests you knew, to pray for them tomorrow.
2027-01-23.question: Do I use my lips for praise and witness?

family.explain: A man could not speak. Jesus healed him and he began to talk! Jesus helps us to speak kindly and to praise God.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and for priests who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we say a thank-you prayer for our parish priest?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Kollam the people still tell of a priest who served them for thirty years and died during an epidemic, visiting the sick. On Kohne Sunday old parishioners light candles at his grave. One said: he taught my whole family to pray; the least I can do is pray for him now.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, our high priest, open our lips to praise you and bless your priests. Amen.
share: We have such a high priest (Hebrews 8:1). Do I trust Christ to intercede for me?
A sketch and shadow of the heavenly one (Hebrews 8:5). Do I see the heavenly reality in the liturgy?
The one who had been mute spoke (Matthew 9:33). Where is Christ asking me to speak?
pm.resp: Christ our high priest, hear us.
interc: For our Pope, bishops and priests.
For departed priests, as we prepare for Kohne Sunday.
For vocations to the priesthood.
For those who cannot speak or hear.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, your Son is our high priest in the heavens. Bless the priests of your Church and open our lips to praise you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Saul the persecutor met the risen Jesus.
He proclaimed the faith he once tried to destroy.
Jesus prayed: that they may all be one.
2027-01-25.action: Pray today for Christians of another Church by name.
2027-01-25.question: Do I work for unity or division in my family and parish?

family.explain: Before he died, Jesus prayed for us: that we may all be one, like a family. When Christians love each other, people believe in Jesus!
family.intention: We pray for all Christians, that they may be one.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be more united as a family this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Adoor, Catholic, Orthodox and Marthoma families share a single cemetery road. Each year during the Unity Week their young people clean it together and pray at its end. An elderly man said: our grandfathers quarrelled over this road; our grandchildren pray on it together. That is Jesus' prayer being answered.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, make us one, as you and the Father are one. Amen.
share: Why do you persecute me? (Acts 9:4). How do I treat Christ in his Church?
Now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy (Galatians 1:23). Whom have I given up on?
That they may all be one (John 17:21). What divides me from others?
interc: For the unity of all Christians.
For the eparchies of Pathanamthitta and Puttur, their bishops, clergy and people.
For those hostile to the Church.
For our separated brothers and sisters in Kerala.
For our group, that we may be one in love.
pm.close: Father, your Son prayed that we may be one. Heal our divisions and make us witnesses of your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: You are a letter of Christ written on hearts.
Our competence is from God.
Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's.
2027-01-26.action: Pray for India and its leaders today.
2027-01-26.question: Do I give God what belongs to God: my whole self?

family.explain: Jesus looked at a coin with the king's picture on it. He said: give the king what has his picture, and give God what has God's picture. We have God's picture in us!
family.intention: We pray for India on Republic Day.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be good citizens and good children of God?”

illus: An illustration

A schoolteacher in Kollam takes her class to hoist the flag every Republic Day and then to the parish church to pray for the country. A boy asked her why both. She said: the flag tells you whose country you serve; the cross tells you whose child you are.

pm.open: Lord, write your Spirit on our hearts and bless our nation. Amen.
share: You are a letter of Christ (2 Corinthians 3:3). What does my life say about Christ?
Our competence is from God (2 Corinthians 3:5). Do I rely on God?
Give to God the things that are God's (Matthew 22:21). What am I holding back from God?
interc: For India on Republic Day.
For the President, Prime Minister and all in authority.
For justice and harmony among all communities.
For the poor and marginalised.
For our group, that we may be faithful citizens and disciples.
pm.close: Father, all authority comes from you. Bless our country and make us your faithful people. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ.
Husbands, love as Christ loved the Church.
Marriage is a great mystery: Christ and the Church.
2027-01-27.action: Do one act of humble service for your spouse or family.
2027-01-27.question: Does my love for my family give itself, as Christ gave himself?

family.explain: St Paul says husbands and wives should love and serve each other the way Jesus loves the Church. Jesus' love is a love that gives everything!
family.intention: We pray for our parents and all married couples.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we serve each other at home today?”

illus: An illustration

An elderly man in Mavelikara fed his wife, paralysed by a stroke, every meal for eleven years. When the parish priest praised him, he said: on our wedding day I was crowned in church as her king. A king serves his kingdom. She is my kingdom.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, faithful Bridegroom, bless our families and teach us self-giving love. Amen.
share: Be subject to one another (Ephesians 5:21). Where do I insist on my own way?
As Christ loved the church (Ephesians 5:25). Does my love cost me something?
A great mystery (Ephesians 5:32). Do I see marriage as holy?
interc: For married couples, that they may grow in faithful love.
For families in crisis.
For those whose marriages are wounded.
For young people preparing for marriage.
For our group, that our homes may be domestic churches.
pm.close: Father, you made marriage a sign of Christ's love for the Church. Strengthen our families in that love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Remember your leaders and imitate their faith.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and forever.
Jesus is the way, the truth and the life.
2027-01-28.action: Pray for a priest who helped your faith.
2027-01-28.question: Do I follow Jesus as the way, or do I make my own road?

family.explain: Jesus told his friends not to be worried, because he is preparing a home for them in heaven. He is the way to get there!
family.intention: We pray for priests, especially those who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Which priest has helped our family? Let us pray for him.”

illus: An illustration

A woman in Thiruvalla keeps a small notebook with the names of every priest who has served her parish since her childhood. Each Kohne week she prays for them one by one. She says: they showed me the way; the least I can do is walk them home with my prayers.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, way, truth and life, lead us to the Father and bless your priests. Amen.
share: Remember your leaders (Hebrews 13:7). Whose faith do I imitate?
The same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:8). Do I trust Christ in times of change?
I am the way (John 14:6). Where do I need his direction?
interc: For departed priests, especially Fr John Kuzhinapurath.
For living priests and bishops.
For students and teachers, through St Thomas Aquinas.
For those troubled in heart.
For our group, that we may share what we have.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the way to you. Keep us faithful on that way until we reach your house. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: To see Jesus is to see the grain of wheat that dies and bears fruit.
Present your bodies as a living sacrifice.
Mar Ignatius wished to be God's wheat for Christ.
2027-01-29.action: Offer today's work to God as a living sacrifice.
2027-01-29.question: What must die in me so that I may bear fruit?

family.explain: A seed must go into the ground before it grows into a big plant with lots of grain. Jesus gave his life for us, and that brought new life to the whole world!
family.intention: We pray for our bishops, especially Joshua Mar Ignathios.
family.ask: Ask: “What small sacrifice can each of us offer to Jesus today?”

illus: An illustration

A paddy farmer in Kuttanad showed his grandson a handful of seed rice. He said: if I keep these in a jar, I will have only these. If I bury them in the mud, I will have a field. He added: Jesus says the same about our lives.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, grain of wheat, make us a living sacrifice and fruitful in your love. Amen.
share: We wish to see Jesus (John 12:21). Do I seek to see Jesus?
Present your bodies as a living sacrifice (Romans 12:1). What can I offer today?
If it dies, it bears much fruit (John 12:24). What do I need to let go of?
interc: For our bishops, especially Joshua Mar Ignathios on his name day.
For persecuted Christians, through Mar Ignatius.
For those who give their lives in hidden service.
For unity with our bishops.
For our group, that we may use our gifts for the Church.
pm.close: Father, your Son died like a grain of wheat and rose to bear fruit. Make our lives fruitful in him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Examine yourselves: Christ is in you.
The tree is known by its fruit.
Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
2027-01-30.action: Make an examination of conscience tonight.
2027-01-30.question: What do my words reveal about my heart?

family.explain: Jesus says a good tree gives good fruit. When our hearts are full of love, we say kind words!
family.intention: We pray that our family may speak kindly to each other.
family.ask: Ask: “What kind words can we say to each other today?”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Kollam put a jar in the kitchen. Each time someone in the family said a harsh word, they put in a coin; each time someone said a kind word, they took one out. At the end of the month the jar was nearly empty. Her son said: our words changed because our hearts changed.

pm.open: Lord, search our hearts and make our words good. Amen.
share: Examine yourselves (2 Corinthians 13:5). Am I living in the faith?
The tree is known by its fruit (Matthew 12:33). What fruit does my life bear?
Every careless word (Matthew 12:36). Which words do I regret?
pm.resp: Lord, set a guard over our mouths.
interc: For honest and kind speech in our homes.
For those hurt by careless words.
For journalists and all who speak in public.
For the Syriac Churches, through Mar Jacob Aphrahat.
For our group, that our words may build up.
pm.close: Father, make our hearts a good treasure and our words a blessing. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed New Year to all of you! On this first day of the year, the Church celebrates the Naming of our Lord. Eight days after his birth, the Child was circumcised and given the name the angel had announced: Jesus.

In Hebrew, Jesus means “the Lord saves”. The angel told Joseph: “you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.” So on New Year's Day the Church does not give us a list of resolutions; she gives us a Name. St Peter says: “There is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.”

St Paul tells us what a real new beginning looks like: put away the old self, and clothe yourselves with the new self, created in the likeness of God. A new calendar does not make a new person. Only Christ makes us new. Let each of us name one old habit to put off, and one virtue to put on, this year.

And like Mary and Joseph, who brought the Child to offer him to the Lord, let us offer this whole year to God: our families, our work, our health, our plans. Today is also the World Day of Peace. May the Prince of Peace give peace to our homes and to our world. Jesus, we begin this year in your Name. Amen.
kids: Children, happy New Year! Today we remember the day baby Jesus got his name. Do you know what “Jesus” means? “God saves!”
Mary and Joseph gave him that name because an angel told them to. Jesus came to save us and help us be good.
This year, let's start every day by saying: “Jesus, I love you!” Let's say it together now: “Jesus, I love you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, we are still in the light of Christmas, and today John the Baptist points to the Child of Bethlehem and says: “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!” The baby in the manger came for a purpose: to give his life for us, as the Passover lamb was given for Israel.

In the evening Gospel the crowds ask John: “What then should we do?” His answer is very simple. “Whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none; whoever has food must do likewise.” To tax collectors: be honest. To soldiers: do not extort. Conversion is not a beautiful feeling; it is a changed way of using what we have.

After Christmas many of us have more than enough: new clothes, sweets, gifts. John asks: where is your second coat? Who needs it? Our readings also show children growing up close to God: Samuel growing in the presence of the Lord, his mother bringing him a little robe each year. Let us help our children grow like that.

And as the new year begins, Isaiah promises: “Those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles.” On Wednesday we celebrate Denho, the Baptism of the Lord. Come, renew your own baptism, and follow the Lamb. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist was Jesus' cousin. When he saw Jesus coming, he said: “Look! The Lamb of God!” He meant that Jesus came to take away all our sins.
People asked John: “What should we do?” He said: “If you have two shirts, give one to someone who has none.”
Do you have a toy or a shirt you could share? Let's say: “Like John, I will share!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Denho, the feast of the manifestation of the Lord. The Child of Bethlehem, hidden for thirty years in Nazareth, comes to the Jordan and is revealed to the world. When he comes up out of the water, the heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father's voice says: “This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.”

John did not want to baptise him: “I need to be baptised by you!” But Jesus went down into the water with sinners. Why? He had no sin to wash away. The Fathers answer: he went down to make the waters holy for us. The Jordan became the source of every baptismal font in the world.

Our Old Testament readings are full of water: Rebekah at the well, a river flowing from the Temple bringing life wherever it goes, Isaiah's joyful promise: “With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.” In our Baptism we drank from those wells. And the same voice spoke over each of us: “You are my beloved child.”

Today, as the waters are blessed, let us renew our baptismal promises with faith. Take the blessed water home; bless your children with it each night. Find out the date of your Baptism and thank God for it every year. Live as beloved children of the Father, filled with the Holy Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, today we remember the day Jesus was baptised in the river Jordan. When he came out of the water, heaven opened!
The Holy Spirit came down like a white dove, and God the Father said: “This is my beloved Son!” Father, Son and Holy Spirit, all together.
When you were baptised, God said: “You are my beloved child!” Do you know your baptism day? Ask your parents tonight! Let's say: “I am God's beloved child!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Wednesday we celebrated Denho, the Baptism of the Lord. Now Jesus begins his work. He goes to Galilee, a region of ordinary working people, and begins to preach: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.” And the first thing he does is call people.

He walks by the lake and sees fishermen at work: Simon and Andrew casting their nets, James and John mending theirs. He says: “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” And immediately they left their nets and followed him. No delay, no long negotiation.

God always calls people at work. Moses was looking after sheep when he saw the burning bush and heard: “Remove your sandals, for the place where you stand is holy ground.” The ordinary place of his work became holy because God was there. Your kitchen, your office, your field can become holy ground too.

What are your nets? Your phone, your worries, your ambitions, your comforts? Jesus does not always ask us to leave our jobs, but he always asks us to put him first. And some of our young people he calls to leave everything for the priesthood or religious life. Let us pray for them, and let us answer him: “Lord, I will follow you.” Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus walked by a big lake and saw fishermen catching fish. He said: “Come, follow me! I will make you fishers of people!”
The fishermen left their nets straight away and went with Jesus. They became his friends, the apostles.
Jesus calls you too: to be his friend and bring others to him. Let's say: “Jesus, I will follow you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today's Gospel tells how one friend brought another to Jesus. Philip found Nathanael and said: “We have found the one Moses and the prophets wrote about: Jesus of Nazareth.” Nathanael laughed: “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?”

Philip did not argue. He simply said: “Come and see.” That is still the best way to bring people to Christ. Not long debates, not pressure, but an invitation: come and see. Come to Qurbono with me. Come to the prayer meeting. Meet him yourself.

When Nathanael came, Jesus said: “I saw you under the fig tree.” Jesus knew him already. Nathanael's doubt melted: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God!” And Jesus promised: “You will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.” He is Jacob's ladder; in him heaven and earth meet. At this altar, today, heaven opens.

Tomorrow the Nineveh fast begins. When Jonah preached, the whole city turned back to God. Let us keep these three days well: fasting, the special prayers, a good Confession. And this week, let each of us say to one person: “Come and see.” Amen.
kids: Children, Philip met Jesus and was so happy! He ran to his friend Nathanael and said: “Come and see Jesus!”
Nathanael came, and Jesus said: “I saw you under the fig tree.” Jesus knew him already! Nathanael believed.
Jesus knows you too, and loves you. Who can you invite to come and meet Jesus? Let's say: “Come and see!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Kohne Sunday, when our Church remembers the priests who have died. Think for a moment of the priests in your own life: the one who baptised you, who gave you your First Holy Communion, who heard your confessions, who blessed your marriage, who buried your parents. Many of them are now with the Lord.

The letter to the Hebrews says: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.” We remember them with gratitude. They were human, with weaknesses like ours, but through their hands Christ gave us his Body and Blood and his forgiveness.

Our reading from Numbers tells how Aaron, the first high priest, died, and Moses placed his vestments on his son Eleazar. The priest dies; the priesthood continues. For Christ is the one eternal High Priest, “the same yesterday and today and forever”. And the Gospel asks every priest one question: were you a faithful and wise servant, giving God's household their food at the proper time?

Today let us offer this Qurbono for our departed priests, that the Lord may say to them: “Well done, good servant.” Let us thank and support our living priests. And let us pray that from our families God may call new priests, to stand at this altar when we are gone. Amen.
kids: Children, who baptised you? A priest! Who gives you Jesus in Holy Communion? A priest!
Today we remember priests who have died and gone to Jesus. We thank God for them and pray that they are happy in heaven.
Let's pray for our parish priest too. Maybe one day God will call one of you to be a priest or sister! Let's say: “Thank you, Jesus, for our priests!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Sunday we remembered our departed priests. Today, Aneede Sunday, we remember all our faithful departed. Let us take a moment of silence and bring to mind those we have lost: a father, a mother, a husband, a wife, a child, a friend.

St Paul writes: we do not want you to grieve “as others do who have no hope”. He does not say “do not grieve”. Jesus himself wept at the tomb of his friend. But our grief has hope, because Christ is risen. Jesus says: “All who are in their graves will hear his voice and will come out.” One day our dead will hear that voice.

Why do we pray for the dead? Our reading from Maccabees says: if Judas had not believed in the resurrection, it would have been foolish to pray for the fallen. The Church has always prayed and offered the Holy Qurbono for the departed, that they may be purified and enter fully into God's joy. St Monica asked her son Augustine only one thing before she died: “Remember me at the altar of the Lord.”

And the evening Gospel reminds us how we ourselves will be judged: “I was hungry and you gave me food… as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me.” Next Sunday the Great Fast begins. Let us enter it remembering that life is short, that love is what remains, and that we too are walking towards the Lord. Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, do you have a grandpa or grandma who has gone to God? Today we remember all the people we love who have died.
We feel sad, but we also have hope, because Jesus rose from the dead and he will bring them to new life.
Tonight, pray for them by name. Let's say: “Jesus, keep them happy with you in heaven!”

homily: Dear friends, today we honour Mar Baselios and Mar Gregorios, two great bishops of Cappadocia in the fourth century. They were close friends who defended faith in the Holy Trinity. Our Catholicos bears the name Baselios, and today is his name day. We pray for him and for the Eparchy of Mavelikara.

In the Gospel Nicodemus, a respected teacher, comes to Jesus by night. Jesus tells him: no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit (John 3:5). Nicodemus is puzzled. How can an old man be born again? Jesus speaks of a birth from above, a gift of God.
In a few days we celebrate Denho, the Baptism of the Lord. Jesus' baptism opens the way for ours. In Baptism we were born of water and Spirit and became children of God.
Jesus also says: just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14). The new life flows from the Cross.

Paul gives Timothy a portrait of a good shepherd: not quarrelsome but kindly to everyone, an apt teacher, patient, correcting opponents with gentleness (2 Timothy 2:24–25). That was Basil and Gregory. May it be our Catholicos, our bishops, our priests, and every parent and teacher. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said we must be born again from water and the Holy Spirit. That happened when you were baptised! Today let us pray for our Catholicos, Baselios Bava.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews 11 is the great hall of faith. Today we hear about the first three heroes. Abel offered God a more acceptable sacrifice. Enoch pleased God and was taken up. Noah, warned about things not yet seen, built an ark and saved his household (Hebrews 11:4–7).

The key sentence is this: without faith it is impossible to please God, for whoever would approach him must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him (Hebrews 11:6). Faith is trusting God's word enough to build an ark before the rain.

In the Gospel Jesus goes up the mountain and gives the Beatitudes. They are the portrait of a person of faith: poor in spirit, merciful, pure in heart, a peacemaker. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God (Matthew 5:8).

Today we remember the prophet Malachi, who promised that the sun of righteousness would rise with healing in its wings (Malachi 4:2), and St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, who lived the Beatitudes among the poor of Kerala, building schools and homes of prayer.
On Wednesday we celebrate Denho, when that Sun rises at the Jordan. Let us choose one Beatitude to live this week, and prepare our hearts to see God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: happy are the kind, the gentle and the peacemakers! Choose one this week. Will you be a peacemaker at home?

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Ephesians that the risen Christ gave gifts to his Church: apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers, to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up the body of Christ (Ephesians 4:11–12). Every gift is for others.
The goal is maturity: speaking the truth in love, we must grow up in every way into him who is the head, into Christ (Ephesians 4:15). Not truth without love, and not love without truth.

In the Gospel Jesus says: do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear. Consider the ravens; consider the lilies. They neither toil nor spin, yet even Solomon in all his glory was not clothed like one of these (Luke 12:22, 27).

Today we remember the erection of our Eparchy of St Mary, Queen of Peace, in the USA and Canada. Many of our families live far from home under heavy pressure. Jesus says to them and to us: your Father knows what you need.
Tonight is the eve of Denho. Tomorrow the Father will speak at the Jordan: this is my beloved Son. Let us lay down our worries tonight and come tomorrow as children who trust their Father. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: look at the flowers! God makes them so beautiful. If God takes care of flowers, he will surely take care of you. Don't be afraid!

homily: Dear friends, on the day after Denho the Syriac Churches praise John the Baptist, who baptised the Lord in the Jordan. Jesus himself speaks his praise.

He asks the crowds: what did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind? (Luke 7:24). No. John was not shaken by public opinion or by Herod's power. Someone dressed in soft robes? No. John lived in poverty.
A prophet? Yes, says Jesus, and more than a prophet. He is the messenger sent ahead to prepare the way. Among those born of women no one is greater than John (Luke 7:28).

Then a surprise: yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he. John stood at the door; by Baptism we have entered. This is not about our merit but about grace. Paul calls himself a servant of the gospel according to the gift of God's grace (Ephesians 3:7).
Let us honour John by being firm in faith, simple in life, and grateful for the Kingdom we have received. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said John the Baptist was very great and strong, like a tree in a storm. Let us be strong for Jesus too!

homily: Dear friends, in the days after Denho the Syriac Churches honour Mar Stephanos, the first martyr. At the Jordan the Baptist saw the heavens open. At his death Stephen sees the same: I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God (Acts 7:56).
Jesus is standing, as if rising to welcome his witness. The council covers their ears and rushes at him. They stone him. A young man named Saul guards their coats.

And Stephen prays as Jesus prayed on the Cross: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. Then he kneels and cries out: Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:59–60). He dies forgiving. Later, that young Saul becomes Paul the Apostle. The martyr's prayer bore fruit.

Jesus had foretold it: I send you prophets, sages, and scribes, some of whom you will kill (Matthew 23:34). Stephen began as a deacon serving tables and ended with the crown of martyrdom. Service and witness are one road.
Today is the name day of Bishop Philipos Mar Stephanos; we pray for him. Let us ask for Stephen's faith to see heaven, his love to forgive, and his humility to serve. Amen.
kids: Children, Stephen loved Jesus very much. Even when people hurt him, he prayed for them. Let us pray for anyone who has hurt us.

homily: Dear friends, the Pharisees and scribes see Jesus' disciples eating with unwashed hands, against the tradition of the elders. They complain. Jesus answers with Isaiah: this people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me (Mark 7:6).

Jesus is not against tradition. Our Church lives by Holy Tradition, received from the Apostles. He is against human customs that replace God's commandment: you abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition (Mark 7:8).
St Paul asks: if some were unfaithful, will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God? By no means! Let God be proved true (Romans 3:3–4). God's faithfulness is stronger than our failures.

A few days ago we celebrated Denho, the Baptism of the Lord. In our Baptism God washed not our hands but our hearts. Let us check our customs and devotions: do they come from the heart? Do they lead us to love God and neighbour? Then they are holy. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said God cares most about a clean heart. Washing hands is good, but a kind and loving heart is even better!

homily: Dear friends, Paul had suffered greatly in Asia. He even felt he had received the sentence of death. Yet he begins his letter with a blessing: blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation (2 Corinthians 1:3).
God consoles us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to console others with the consolation we ourselves have received. Our healed wounds become a ministry.
Paul says his trials taught him to rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead (2 Corinthians 1:9). Suffering strips away false supports and leaves us leaning on God alone.

Today we remember Mar Gregorios of Nyssa, brother of Mar Baselios, who taught that the soul is always growing toward God. Christ gives the Spirit without measure (John 3:34). Let us receive God's comfort, pass it on, and keep growing in his love. Amen.
kids: Children, when you are sad, God comforts you. Then you can comfort a friend who is sad. Who can you cheer up today?

homily: Dear friends, Paul says: we do not proclaim ourselves; we proclaim Jesus Christ as Lord and ourselves as your slaves for Jesus' sake (2 Corinthians 4:5). The minister is a window, not a picture.

The same God who said at creation, let light shine out of darkness, has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ (2 Corinthians 4:6). In Denho we gaze at that face.

In the Gospel, they watch to see if Jesus will heal on the sabbath. He asks: which of you would not lift a sheep out of a pit? How much more valuable is a human being than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the sabbath (Matthew 12:12). He heals the withered hand.
Mar Thevodosios the Abbot built houses for the sick, the old and the poor beside his monastery. Prayer and mercy belong together. Let our Sundays be days of both. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus healed a man's hand on God's day. Sunday is a good day to help someone! Whom will you help this Sunday?

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells Timothy: I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone, for kings and all who are in high positions (1 Timothy 2:1–2). Even for rulers who were persecuting Christians.

The reason: God desires everyone to be saved. There is one God; there is also one mediator between God and humankind, Christ Jesus, himself human (1 Timothy 2:4–5). Our prayer must be as wide as God's love.
Jesus warns us against judging. Why do you see the speck in your neighbor's eye, but do not notice the log in your own eye? (Matthew 7:3). We can be very sharp about others and blind about ourselves.
We cannot pray sincerely for someone and condemn him at the same time. Let us replace judgement with intercession: pray today for one person you find hard to bear. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a funny story about a man with a log in his eye! Before we say someone is bad, let us look at ourselves. And let us pray for everyone.

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes the heart of the Gospel: all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; they are now justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus (Romans 3:23–24). Salvation is a gift, not a wage.

In the Gospel Jesus says to his friends: do not fear those who kill the body, and after that can do nothing more (Luke 12:4). He reminds them: God does not forget even a sparrow. Even the hairs of your head are all counted. Do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows (Luke 12:7).

Today we remember the Forty Martyrs of Sinai, monks killed by raiders while at prayer, and St Devasahayam, the Indian layman who gave his life for Christ in 1752. They feared God, and so they feared nothing else.
Let us receive God's grace with gratitude and live our faith without fear. Amen.
kids: Children, God knows how many hairs are on your head! He takes care of you. Do not be afraid to say you love Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, today our tradition remembers the Mother of God for the seeds. At sowing time farmers brought their seed to be blessed and entrusted the harvest to Mary's prayers.

Paul says: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. God loves a cheerful giver (2 Corinthians 9:6–7). Generosity is like sowing.
And God is the true giver: he who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed (2 Corinthians 9:10). All growth is grace.

In the Gospel Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19). She is the good soil where the Word was sown. Let us pray for our farmers and for Muvattupuzha eparchy, and let our hearts receive the Word as Mary did. Amen.
kids: Children, a tiny seed can become a big plant! Mary kept God's words in her heart like seeds. Let us keep Jesus' words in our hearts too.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews says: remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). Today we remember St Peter in chains, and Bishop Geevarghese Mar Divannasios, who served our Church and went home to God in 2018.
Leaders come and go. But Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:8). The faith they handed on is anchored in him.
Jesus asks: who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household? Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives (Matthew 24:45–46).
Each of us has been put in charge of something: a family, a job, a ministry. Let us be faithful in it, offer God the sacrifice of praise, and share what we have. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told about a servant who did his job well even when nobody was watching. Do your homework and chores well, for Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, the fast of the Ninevites begins with a prophet running away. God says to Jonah: go to Nineveh. But Jonah set out to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD (Jonah 1:3). The storm rises, the pagan sailors pray, and the prophet sleeps.
We are often like Jonah. We know what God wants and we go the other way. These three days are our chance to stop running.

Paul shows us the opposite: Christ humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross (Philippians 2:8). And Jesus calls himself the sign of Jonah: three days in the heart of the earth, then the Resurrection (Matthew 12:40).

Today we remember Moran Mor Cyril Baselios and Joseph Mar Severios, shepherds of our Church. Remember your leaders, says Hebrews, and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). Let us turn the ship around and walk with Christ. Amen.
