kids: Children, Jonah ran away from God, but God did not give up on him! These three days, let us say sorry and come back to God.

homily: Dear friends, on the second day of the fast Jonah obeys. He enters Nineveh and cries out. And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth (Jonah 3:5).

The king commands: all shall turn from their evil ways and from the violence that is in their hands (Jonah 3:8). Nineveh fasted with its hands as well as its stomach. Our fast too must change how we treat others.
Jesus warns that his coming will be like the days of Noah, when people did not notice until the flood came. Keep awake therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming (Matthew 24:42).

Paul tells us how the watchful live: let love be genuine; rejoice in hope, be patient in suffering, persevere in prayer (Romans 12:9, 12). With Mar Macarios, let us keep the faith and keep awake. Amen.
kids: Children, the people of Nineveh stopped doing bad things and said sorry to God. Let us be kind at home today, and say sorry if we hurt someone.

homily: Dear friends, today we hear Jonah praying from the belly of the fish. At the bottom of the sea, with weeds around his head, he prays: I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me; out of the belly of Sheol I cried, and you heard my voice (Jonah 2:2).
There is no depth where God cannot hear us. On the third day the fish brought Jonah to dry land. The Fathers saw here the death and Resurrection of Christ, and our own Baptism.

In the Gospel Jesus says: unless you repent, you will all perish (Luke 13:3). We often think repentance is for others. Jesus says it is for me, now. Paul adds: you are all children of light and children of the day (1 Thessalonians 5:5).
Today we honour St Sebastian, who served Christ more than Caesar and did not fear death. On this last day of the fast, let us pray from our depths, repent honestly and stand firm. Amen.
kids: Children, Jonah prayed to God from inside a big fish, and God heard him! God hears us wherever we are.

homily: Dear friends, the fast ends with a surprise. Nineveh repents and is spared, and Jonah is angry. God asks him: is it right for you to be angry? (Jonah 4:4). And the book ends with God's question to all of us: should I not be concerned about Nineveh, that great city? (Jonah 4:11).
The fast is not finished until our heart becomes as wide as God's mercy, even for those we dislike.

The other readings show us intercessors. Abraham pleads for Sodom: suppose ten are found there (Genesis 18:32). Paul, once a persecutor, writes that God was pleased to reveal his Son to me (Galatians 1:15–16).
And Jesus says: something greater than Jonah is here! (Luke 11:32). With St Agnes, who loved Christ with her whole young heart, let us leave the fast with wide hearts and listening ears. Amen.
kids: Children, God loved all the people of Nineveh, even their animals! God wants us to love everyone, even people who are not nice to us.

homily: Dear friends, today we remember Mar Timotheos, the young disciple of St Paul. Paul charges him: pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, gentleness. Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of the eternal life, to which you were called (1 Timothy 6:11–12).
Timothy was young, timid and often sick, yet he became a shepherd of the church in Ephesus. God's strength works through our weakness.

In the Gospel Jesus says: I have come not to abolish but to fulfill (Matthew 5:17). The Old Testament is not thrown away; Christ fulfils it. Timothy learned the Scriptures from his mother and grandmother.
Let our homes too be schools of the word. Let us fight the good fight and hand on the faith. Amen.
kids: Children, Timothy learned about God from his mother and grandmother. Who teaches you about God? Thank them today!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews tells us the main point: we have such a high priest, one who is seated at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens (Hebrews 8:1). He is the mediator of a better covenant (Hebrews 8:6).
The old priesthood was a sketch and shadow; Christ is the reality. Tomorrow, Kohne Sunday, we pray for our departed priests, who shared in Christ's priesthood with all their human weakness.
In the Gospel a mute man is healed and speaks, and the crowds are amazed (Matthew 9:33). Christ opens mouths for praise.
Let us use our lips for praise and witness, and tomorrow let us remember with gratitude the priests who taught us to pray. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus helped a man who could not speak to talk again! Let us use our mouths to say kind words and to praise God.

homily: Dear friends, today we keep the Conversion of St Paul. Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the disciples, is thrown down by a light from heaven and hears: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? (Acts 9:4).

Paul does not hide his past: I was violently persecuting the church of God and was trying to destroy it. Then people said: the one who formerly was persecuting us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy (Galatians 1:13, 23). No one is beyond grace.
The Gospel is Jesus' prayer: that they may all be one, so that the world may believe that you have sent me (John 17:21). Division hides Christ; unity reveals him.
Our Church was born of the longing for unity. Today we thank God also for the eparchies of Pathanamthitta and Puttur, and pray that we may always be a bridge of communion. Amen.
kids: Children, Saul was against Jesus, but Jesus changed him into St Paul! Jesus prays that all Christians may be one big family.

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the Corinthians: you show that you are a letter of Christ, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, on tablets of human hearts (2 Corinthians 3:3). The best proof of the Gospel is a changed community.
And he adds: our competence is from God (2 Corinthians 3:5).

In the Gospel, on this Republic Day, Jesus says: give to the emperor the things that are the emperor's, and to God the things that are God's (Matthew 22:21). The coin bears Caesar's image; we bear God's.

So we are loyal citizens: we pay taxes, obey just laws, serve the common good and pray for our leaders. But the State is not God. Belonging to God gives us courage to stand for justice and for the freedom of conscience our Constitution guarantees to all. Amen.
kids: Children, the coin had the king's picture, but you have God's picture in you! Let us pray for India today and give our hearts to God.

homily: Dear friends, Paul begins: be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ (Ephesians 5:21). Christian marriage is mutual self-giving, not domination.
Then he says: husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her (Ephesians 5:25). The measure of love is the cross.

Quoting Genesis, the two will become one flesh, he adds: this is a great mystery, and I am applying it to Christ and the church (Ephesians 5:32). In the Gospel Jesus teaches that this bond is not to be broken.
In our tradition the Crowning shows husband and wife as king and queen of a domestic church. Let us pray for all couples and for wounded families, that they may find Christ's mercy and truth. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus loves his Church like a good husband loves his wife. Let us pray for our mummy and daddy, and help them at home today!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews says: remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). In this Kohne week we remember departed priests, among them Fr John Kuzhinapurath.
Leaders pass, but Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:8). Our sacrifices are praise and sharing: do not neglect to do good and to share what you have (Hebrews 13:16).
In the Gospel Jesus says: do not let your hearts be troubled. Thomas asks: how can we know the way? Jesus answers: I am the way, and the truth, and the life (John 14:6).
St Thomas Aquinas gave his mind to the Truth and his heart to the Life. Let us follow the Way, praise God, share with others and pray for our priests. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: I am the way! He shows us how to go to heaven. Let us pray for the priests who teach us about Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, some Greeks say to Philip: sir, we wish to see Jesus (John 12:21). Jesus answers by speaking of his death: unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit (John 12:24).
To see Jesus is to see the cross, and to follow him is to share it. Paul says: present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God (Romans 12:1).
Today we honour Mar Ignatius Noorono, bishop of Antioch, who on the way to martyrdom in Rome wrote that he wished to be God's wheat, ground by the teeth of beasts, to become the pure bread of Christ.
We pray too for Joshua Mar Ignathios on his name day. Let us offer ourselves as a living sacrifice, and use our gifts as members of one body in Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, a seed goes into the ground and grows into a big plant! Jesus gave his life for us, and we can give little gifts of love to him every day.

homily: Dear friends, Paul says: examine yourselves to see whether you are living in the faith. Do you not realize that Jesus Christ is in you? (2 Corinthians 13:5). On the eve of the Lord's Day, it is good to look into our hearts.
Jesus says: the tree is known by its fruit. The good person brings good things out of a good treasure (Matthew 12:33, 35). Our words reveal our hearts.
He warns that we will give an account for every careless word (Matthew 12:36). Words can heal or wound.
Today we remember Mar Jacob Aphrahat, the Persian Sage, who taught that the heart is the temple where Christ dwells. Let us examine our hearts tonight, and fill them with good treasure. Amen.
kids: Children, a good tree gives good fruit, and a good heart gives kind words! Let us say only kind words today.

intro: Theme: “Begin the year in the name of Jesus.”
On the eighth day the Child received the name the angel had given: Jesus, “God saves”. We begin the new year not with luck or fear but with a name: the name above every name.

points.h: The name that reveals who he is
sub: At the burning bush God revealed his name to Moses: a name to be remembered for all generations.
In Jesus that name becomes a person: “God saves”.
Mary and Joseph obey the angel: they give the name God chose.
q: This is my name forever, and this my title for all generations.
After eight days had passed, it was time to circumcise the child; and he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
points.apply: Say the name of Jesus with reverence; never use it carelessly.

points.h: There is no other saving name
sub: The prophets promised: whoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
Peter proclaimed: there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved.
In every need of the coming year, call on this name with faith.
q: Then everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved.
There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.
points.apply: Make the short prayer “Jesus, I trust in you” your companion this year.

points.h: A new year, a new self
sub: The priests of Israel blessed the people by placing God's name upon them.
Mary and Joseph presented the Child to the Lord; we present this new year to him.
St Paul tells us to put off the old self and put on the new, created in righteousness and holiness.
q: The LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you; the LORD lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
Clothe yourselves with the new self, created according to the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness.
points.apply: Write one resolution for the year that will make you more like Christ, and offer it at the altar today.

concl: Whatever this year brings, it is placed under the name of Jesus.
Let us begin it blessed, cleansed and renewed, calling on the name that saves.
2027-01-01.resolve: Bless your family with the words of Numbers 6:24–26 at the start of each month this year.

intro: Theme: “Behold the Lamb of God.”
John the Baptist points away from himself to Jesus: “Here is the Lamb of God.” He also tells ordinary people how to prepare for him: by concrete repentance in daily life.

sub: Isaiah saw a silent Servant led like a lamb to the slaughter.
John recognises Jesus as the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world.
The Church calls Christ the Lamb in her liturgy; in the Holy Qurbono we receive the Lamb who was sacrificed for us.
q: Like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
points.apply: Look at the Holy Mysteries at the elevation and say in your heart: “Lamb of God, have mercy on me.”

sub: The crowds ask: “What then should we do?”
John's answers are practical: share your coat and food; collect only what is just; do not threaten or accuse falsely.
Isaiah too: cease to do evil, learn to do good, defend the orphan and the widow.
q: Cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow.
And the crowds asked him, “What then should we do?” In reply he said to them, “Whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none; and whoever has food must do likewise.”
points.apply: Give away one good garment or one day's food to someone in need this week.

sub: The boy Samuel grew in favour with God and people while serving in the Temple.
John saw the Spirit descend and testified: “This is the Son of God.”
Every Christian is called to grow in faith and to bear witness, not to himself, but to Christ.
q: Now the boy Samuel continued to grow both in stature and in favor with the LORD and with the people.
And I myself have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.
points.apply: Speak of Jesus simply to one person this week: what he means to you.

concl: John's whole life is a finger pointing to Christ.
Let our lives too say to others: “Behold the Lamb of God.”
2027-01-03.resolve: Pray each night this week: “Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.”

intro: Theme: “The heavens opened: the Son, the Spirit, the Father, and our Baptism.”
Denho means “dawning” or “manifestation”. At the Jordan Jesus is revealed as the beloved Son, the Spirit rests on him, and the Father speaks. Today we also remember our own Baptism.

points.h: The sinless One enters our waters
sub: John protests: “I need to be baptized by you.”
Jesus answers: “Let it be so now; it is proper for us to fulfil all righteousness”: he stands with sinners.
The Fathers say: he did not need the waters to make him holy; he made the waters holy for us.
q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
But Jesus answered him, “Let it be so now; for it is proper for us in this way to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he consented.
points.apply: Thank God for the humility of Christ, who stands in line with sinners.

sub: The heavens are torn apart: God's distance is overcome.
The Spirit descends like a dove; the Father's voice declares the beloved Son.
Isaiah's servant, filled with the Spirit, is revealed: Jesus is the Christ, the Anointed.
q: Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.

And just as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him. And a voice came from heaven, “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
points.apply: Make the sign of the Cross today slowly, thinking of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

points.h: Our Baptism: drawing water from the wells of salvation
sub: Isaiah promised joy from the wells of salvation.
In Baptism the same Spirit came upon us; in Chrismation we were sealed with holy Myron.
St Paul's disciples at Ephesus received the Spirit when hands were laid on them.
q: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
He saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Find out the date of your Baptism and celebrate it every year.

concl: At the Jordan heaven opened; at our Baptism heaven opened for us.
Let us live as beloved children of the Father, filled with the Spirit, following the Son.
2027-01-06.resolve: Renew your baptismal promises at home this week: reject sin and profess the Creed.

intro: Theme: “Follow me.”
After his Baptism Jesus begins his ministry in Galilee. Light dawns on a land in darkness, and ordinary fishermen hear a call that changes their lives. The same call reaches us.

sub: Jesus begins not in Jerusalem but in “Galilee of the Gentiles”, a mixed and despised region.
Isaiah's promise is fulfilled: a light for the nations.
Christ still begins where people sit in darkness: in our struggles and our neighbourhoods.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light, and for those who sat in the region and shadow of death light has dawned.
points.apply: Pray for one person you know who is in darkness: illness, addiction, despair.

sub: God called Moses by name from the bush, and he answered: “Here I am.”
Jesus calls fishermen at their work: “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.”
They leave their nets “immediately”: a call delayed is often a call lost.
q: God called to him out of the bush, “Moses, Moses!” And he said, “Here I am.”
And he said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
points.apply: Ask: what “net” holds me back from following Jesus more closely? Leave it this week.

points.h: A community born of the call
sub: Those who answered became the first Church: teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer.
God heals the brokenhearted and gathers his people.
Every call to follow Christ is also a call into his Church.
q: He heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds.
They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.
points.apply: Join one parish activity (prayer group, catechism, charity) this month. Pray for vocations.

concl: The Light has come, the call has been given, and the community is gathered.
Let us answer like Moses, “Here I am”, and like the apostles, leave our nets to follow him.
2027-01-10.resolve: Pray daily this week for priestly and religious vocations from your parish.

intro: Theme: “Come and see.”
Philip finds Nathanael and tells him about Jesus. Nathanael doubts: “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip does not argue; he invites: “Come and see.” Faith grows through encounter.

sub: Nathanael's question is honest; God is not afraid of our questions.
Wisdom promises that those who seek diligently will find.
The best answer to doubt is an invitation to meet Christ in Scripture, in the Qurbono and in a living community.
q: I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently find me.
Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
points.apply: Invite one person who has drifted away to come with you to Sunday Qurbono.

sub: Jesus praises Nathanael: “an Israelite in whom there is no deceit.”
God says: “I am the LORD; I sanctify you”: holiness begins with an honest heart.
Jesus already knew Nathanael under the fig tree; nothing is hidden from him.
q: You shall not profane my holy name, that I may be sanctified among the people of Israel: I am the LORD; I sanctify you.
When Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him, he said of him, “Here is truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit!”
points.apply: Remove one falsehood from your life this week: a lie, a pretence, a double life.

points.h: Heaven opened: Christ is the ladder
sub: Jacob dreamed of a ladder with angels ascending and descending.
Jesus says: you will see heaven opened and angels on the Son of Man: he is the meeting place of heaven and earth.
In the Holy Qurbono heaven opens; we join the angels in praise.
q: And he dreamed that there was a ladder set up on the earth, the top of it reaching to heaven; and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.
Very truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
points.apply: At the Sanctus, remember that you are singing with the angels.

concl: Nathanael moved from doubt to confession: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God!”
Let us come and see, let our hearts be without deceit, and find in Christ the open heaven.
2027-01-17.resolve: Read John 1:35–51 slowly once this week and ask: where is Jesus inviting me to “come and see”?

intro: Theme: “Remembering the priests who served us.”
On Kohne Sunday the Church remembers her departed priests. We thank God for them, we pray for them, and we reflect on the gift of the priesthood that continues among us.

sub: On Mount Hor Moses took Aaron's vestments and put them on Eleazar: the ministry continues after death.
Every priest is taken from among the people and appointed for the people, to offer gifts and sacrifices.
The priests who baptised us, absolved us and fed us with the Eucharist have handed on Christ's priesthood to the next generation.
q: Moses stripped Aaron of his vestments, and put them on his son Eleazar; and Aaron died there on the top of the mountain.
Every high priest chosen from among mortals is put in charge of things pertaining to God on their behalf, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
points.apply: Remember by name the priests who baptised you, gave you First Communion, married you or buried your loved ones.

points.h: Faithful stewards of the Master's gift
sub: Aaron was anointed to minister to the Lord and bless the people in his name.
In the parable of the pounds, the faithful servant is praised for trading with what he received.
Priests are judged by faithfulness, not success; so are all of us in our vocations.
q: Moses ordained him, and anointed him with holy oil; it was an everlasting covenant for him and for his descendants … to minister to the Lord and serve as priest and bless his people in his name.
He said to him, “Well done, good slave! Because you have been trustworthy in a very small thing, take charge of ten cities.”
points.apply: Encourage a priest this week with a word of thanks, and pray for one who is struggling.

sub: Judas Maccabeus offered sacrifice for the dead, “a holy and pious thought”.
The Church prays for the faithful departed, that they may be purified and enter God's rest.
Our prayers and Holy Qurbono offered for departed priests are an act of gratitude and charity.
q: But if he was looking to the splendid reward that is laid up for those who fall asleep in godliness, it was a holy and pious thought. Therefore he made atonement for the dead, so that they might be delivered from their sin.
Blessed are the dead who from now on die in the Lord. “Yes,” says the Spirit, “they will rest from their labors, for their deeds follow them.”
points.apply: Have a Holy Qurbono offered, or pray a Rosary, for a departed priest.

concl: The priests we remember today gave their lives so that Christ might be present among us.
Let us thank God for them, pray for their eternal rest, and pray that the Lord will send good and holy priests to his Church.
2027-01-24.resolve: Visit the grave of a priest in your parish cemetery and pray for him.

intro: Theme: “From death to life.”
On Aneede Sunday we remember all our departed: parents, grandparents, friends. We do not come as people without hope. We come to pray for them and to learn from them how to live.

points.h: In Christ, death is a passage to life
sub: Jacob ended his blessing, breathed his last and was “gathered to his people”.
Jesus promises: whoever hears his word and believes has already passed from death to life.
Our departed are not lost; they are on the way home, and we pray that they reach it.
q: When Jacob ended his charge to his sons, he drew up his feet into the bed, breathed his last, and was gathered to his people.
Very truly, I tell you, anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life.
points.apply: Name your departed loved ones in prayer each day this week.

sub: Hezekiah, facing death, turned to God and found mercy.
St Paul does not forbid grief; he forbids grief without hope.
The Church prays for the dead, that they may be purified and see God; this is an act of love (CCC 1032).
q: Surely it was for my welfare that I had great bitterness; but you have held back my life from the pit of destruction, for you have cast all my sins behind your back.

We do not want you to be uninformed … about those who have died, so that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope. For since we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so, through Jesus, God will bring with him those who have died.
points.apply: Have a Holy Qurbono offered for your departed, and visit the cemetery with your family.

points.h: We will be judged by love
sub: At the last judgment the King asks about the hungry, the stranger, the sick and the prisoner.
Proverbs says kindness to the poor is a loan to the Lord.
The best way to honour our dead is to live the works of mercy they taught us.
q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and will be repaid in full.
Truly I tell you, just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.
points.apply: Do one work of mercy this week in memory of a departed loved one.

concl: The dead hear the voice of the Son of God; those who have done good will rise to life.
Let us pray for our departed with faith and live with charity, so that one day we may meet them in the Father's house.
2027-01-31.resolve: Pray “Eternal rest grant to them, O Lord” for the departed after each meal this week.

intro: Theme: “No one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.”
New birth from above, the lifted-up Son, and gentle shepherds.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
Jesus answered, “Very truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises before Denho.

q: And the LORD said to Moses, “Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.”
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up,
points.apply: Spend a few minutes looking at the Cross in silence today.

sub: Firm in truth, kind to all.
q: A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
And the Lord's servant must not be quarrelsome but kindly to everyone, an apt teacher, patient, correcting opponents with gentleness.
points.apply: Pray for our Catholicos and correct others gently.

concl: Born of water and Spirit, we look to the Cross.
Like Basil and Gregory, let us be firm in faith and gentle in love.
2027-01-02.resolve: Pray each day this week for our Catholicos and bishops.

intro: Theme: “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.”
Faith that pleases God, the Beatitudes, and the rising Sun.

q: Enoch walked with God; then he was no more, because God took him.
And without faith it is impossible to please God, for whoever would approach him must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.
points.apply: Act today on one word of God you have been postponing.

points.h: Blessed are the pure in heart
q: Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place? Those who have clean hands and pure hearts, who do not lift up their souls to what is false, and do not swear deceitfully.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
points.apply: Go to confession before Denho.

sub: The Sun rises at the Jordan.
q: But for you who revere my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings. You shall go out leaping like calves from the stall.
You are the light of the world. A city built on a hill cannot be hid.
points.apply: Light a lamp at home for Denho.

concl: Faith, purity of heart and light belong together.
The Sun of righteousness is about to rise at the Jordan.
2027-01-04.resolve: Live one Beatitude deliberately this week.

intro: Theme: “Consider the lilies.”
Gifts for the body, growth into Christ, freedom from worry.

q: The spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
The gifts he gave were that some would be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors and teachers, to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up the body of Christ,
points.apply: Offer one gift to serve your parish this month.

q: The righteous flourish like the palm tree, and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
But speaking the truth in love, we must grow up in every way into him who is the head, into Christ,
points.apply: Speak one needed truth this week, gently.

q: Cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you; he will never permit the righteous to be moved.
He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
points.apply: Entrust one worry to God tonight.

concl: The Father who clothes the lilies speaks tomorrow at the Jordan.
Come to Denho free of worry, ready to grow.
2027-01-05.resolve: Pray tonight for families in the diaspora.

intro: Theme: “Among those born of women no one is greater than John.”
The praise of the Baptist and the grace of the Kingdom.

q: The Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;
When John's messengers had gone, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?
points.apply: Refuse one compromise with the truth today.

q: Lo, I will send you the prophet Elijah before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
I tell you, among those born of women no one is greater than John; yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
points.apply: Thank God for someone who prepared the way of Christ for you.

sub: Paul, the least of the saints.
We are sent to walk the way.
q: But the LORD said to me, “Do not say, ‘I am only a boy’; for you shall go to all to whom I send you, and you shall speak whatever I command you.
Of this gospel I have become a servant according to the gift of God's grace that was given me by the working of his power.
points.apply: Share your faith with one person this week.

concl: John was great; grace makes us greater still.
Let us walk the way he prepared.
2027-01-07.resolve: Thank God each night this week for your Baptism.

intro: Theme: “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
Stephen sees heaven open, forgives, and shows that service and witness are one road.

q: As I watched in the night visions, I saw one like a human being coming with the clouds of heaven. And he came to the Ancient One and was presented before him.
But filled with the Holy Spirit, he gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
points.apply: Look to heaven in prayer in your next trial.

q: Into your hand I commit my spirit; you have redeemed me, O LORD, faithful God.

While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Then he knelt down and cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” When he had said this, he died.
points.apply: Pray by name for someone who has hurt you.

q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
Now, brothers and sisters, you know that members of the household of Stephanas were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints;
points.apply: Offer one service to the parish this week.

concl: The first martyr shows the whole Christian life: faith, forgiveness, service.
His prayer converted Saul; ours can change hearts too.
2027-01-08.resolve: Forgive one person from the heart this week.

intro: Theme: “Let God be proved true.”
God's faithfulness, God's commandment, and the washing of the heart.

sub: His mercies are new each morning.
q: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases, his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
What if some were unfaithful? Will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God?
points.apply: Thank God for one sign of his faithfulness.

q: The Lord said: Because these people draw near with their mouths and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their worship of me is a human commandment learned by rote;
You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition.
points.apply: Renew one devotion so that it comes from the heart.

q: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and put a new and right spirit within me.
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
points.apply: Pray Psalm 51 slowly tonight.

concl: God is faithful even when we are not.
Let our traditions be the clothing of a loving heart.
2027-01-09.resolve: Go to Qurbono tomorrow with a renewed heart.

intro: Theme: “The Father of mercies and the God of all consolation.”
Consoled to console; trusting the God who raises the dead.

q: Comfort, O comfort my people, says your God.

Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation, who consoles us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to console those who are in any affliction with the consolation with which we ourselves are consoled by God.
points.apply: Comfort one suffering person this week.

points.h: Relying on God who raises the dead
q: For you have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, my feet from stumbling.
Indeed, we felt that we had received the sentence of death so that we would rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead.
points.apply: Hand over one fear to God in prayer today.

q: Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took some of the spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders; and when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied. But they did not do so again.
He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.
points.apply: Add five minutes to your daily prayer.

concl: God consoles us so that we may console.
With Mar Gregorios, let us keep growing in God.
2027-01-11.resolve: Visit or call a grieving person this week.

intro: Theme: “It is lawful to do good on the sabbath.”
The light of God's glory in Christ's face, shining through works of mercy.

sub: A new creation in our hearts.
q: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.
For it is the God who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Spend a few minutes before an icon of Christ today.

q: Thus says the LORD: Do not let the wise boast in their wisdom, do not let the mighty boast in their might, do not let the wealthy boast in their wealth;
For we do not proclaim ourselves; we proclaim Jesus Christ as Lord and ourselves as your slaves for Jesus' sake.
points.apply: Speak of Christ rather than yourself in one conversation.

sub: A human being more than a sheep.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
How much more valuable is a human being than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the sabbath.”
points.apply: Do one work of mercy this Sunday.

concl: God's light shines in Christ's face and through our deeds.
Prayer and mercy belong together, as Mar Thevodosios showed.
2027-01-12.resolve: Make next Sunday a day of worship and mercy.

intro: Theme: “Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.”
Prayer as wide as God's will to save; judgement replaced by intercession.

q: But seek the welfare of the city where I have sent you into exile, and pray to the LORD on its behalf, for in its welfare you will find your welfare.

First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone, for kings and all who are in high positions, so that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and dignity.
points.apply: Pray daily this week for our leaders by name.

sub: God desires all to be saved.
q: There is no umpire between us, who might lay his hand on us both.
For there is one God; there is also one mediator between God and humankind, Christ Jesus, himself human,
points.apply: Thank Jesus for standing between you and the Father.

q: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not look on his appearance or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for the LORD does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.”
Why do you see the speck in your neighbor's eye, but do not notice the log in your own eye?
points.apply: Pray for the person you most often criticise.

concl: Intercession and condemnation cannot live in the same heart.
Let our prayer be as wide as God's love.
2027-01-13.resolve: Replace one criticism each day with a prayer.

intro: Theme: “Do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.”
Grace given freely; courage of the martyrs.

q: Do not enter into judgment with your servant, for no one living is righteous before you.
since all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; they are now justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
points.apply: Thank God for one undeserved gift today.

q: I, I am he who comforts you; why then are you afraid of a mere mortal who must die, a human being who fades like grass?
“I tell you, my friends, do not fear those who kill the body, and after that can do nothing more.
points.apply: Do not hide your faith today.

q: For it was you who formed my inward parts; you knit me together in my mother's womb.
But even the hairs of your head are all counted. Do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.
points.apply: Rest in God's care when you are anxious.

concl: Grace frees us from fear and pride.
The martyrs show what trust in God can do.
2027-01-14.resolve: Pray this week for persecuted Christians.

intro: Theme: “God loves a cheerful giver.”
Sowing generously, God's gift of growth, Mary the good soil.

q: Some give freely, yet grow all the richer; others withhold what is due, and only suffer want.
The point is this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
points.apply: Give cheerfully to someone in need this week.

q: As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, shall not cease.”
He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
points.apply: Pray for farmers and a good harvest.

q: For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater,
But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
points.apply: Ponder one Gospel verse each day.

concl: God gives the seed; we sow generously.
Mary shows how the Word bears fruit.
2027-01-15.resolve: Support a farmer or share food with the hungry this week.

intro: Theme: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
Remembering our leaders, trusting the unchanging Lord, serving faithfully.

q: Remember the days of old, consider the years long past; ask your father, and he will inform you; your elders, and they will tell you.
Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.
points.apply: Pray for a departed priest or teacher who formed you.

sub: Put in charge of the household.
q: So Joseph found favor in his sight and attended him; he made him overseer of his house and put him in charge of all that he had.

“Who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give the other slaves their allowance of food at the proper time? Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives.
points.apply: Do your daily duties well, as for the Lord.

q: Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High.

Through him, then, let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name. Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.
points.apply: Share something with someone in need this week.

concl: Leaders pass; Christ remains.
Let him find us faithful at our work.
2027-01-16.resolve: Pray this week for all our bishops and priests, living and departed.

intro: Theme: “Let the same mind be in you that was in Christ Jesus.”
Jonah runs; Christ obeys; the sign of Jonah is the Resurrection.

q: But Jonah set out to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish; so he paid his fare and went on board, to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.
Let the same mind be in you that was in Christ Jesus,
points.apply: Stop avoiding one thing God asks of you.

q: Where can I go from your spirit? Or where can I flee from your presence?
he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death— even death on a cross.
points.apply: Accept one humbling thing without complaint.

q: But the LORD provided a large fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.
points.apply: Bring a dead area of your life to the risen Christ.

concl: The fast begins by stopping our flight.
The obedient Christ is our sign of hope.
2027-01-18.resolve: Keep the three days' fast with prayer and almsgiving.

intro: Theme: “Keep awake therefore.”
Nineveh's turning, the watchful heart, and genuine love.

q: Yet even now, says the LORD, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning; rend your hearts and not your clothing.
Let love be genuine; hate what is evil, hold fast to what is good;
points.apply: Put right one injustice this week.

q: Noah did this; he did all that God commanded him.
Keep awake therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
points.apply: Examine your conscience each night of the fast.

q: Seek the LORD while he may be found, call upon him while he is near;
Rejoice in hope, be patient in suffering, persevere in prayer.
points.apply: Pray the evening prayer with your family.

concl: A true fast turns us from evil.
The watchful live in genuine love and prayer.
2027-01-19.resolve: Make peace with one person before the fast ends.

intro: Theme: “I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me.”
The prayer from the depths, the call to repent, and the courage of St Sebastian.

sub: In the belly of the fish.
q: Out of the depths I cry to you, O LORD. Lord, hear my voice! Let your ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications!
Therefore we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
points.apply: Bring your deepest trouble to God in prayer tonight.

q: Cast away from you all the transgressions that you have committed against me, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit! Why will you die, O house of Israel?
No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all perish as they did.
points.apply: Make your confession before the fast ends.

q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
points.apply: Stand firm in your faith at work or school.

concl: No depth is beyond God's hearing.
Repent now, and live as children of the light.
2027-01-20.resolve: Make a good confession before the fast ends.

intro: Theme: “Something greater than Jonah is here!”
The fast ends: a wide heart, prayer for others, and Christ the true sign.

sub: A heart as wide as mercy.
q: And should I not be concerned about Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons who do not know their right hand from their left, and also many animals?”
This is right and is acceptable in the sight of God our Savior, who desires everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
points.apply: Pray for someone you find hard to forgive.

q: Then he said, “Oh do not let the Lord be angry if I speak just once more. Suppose ten are found there.” He answered, “For the sake of ten I will not destroy it.”
The prayer of the righteous is powerful and effective.
points.apply: Pray for your town by name each day this week.

q: But I trusted in your steadfast love; my heart shall rejoice in your salvation.
The people of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and see, something greater than Jonah is here!
points.apply: Give Christ more attention than Nineveh gave Jonah: read a Gospel passage daily.

concl: The fast is complete when our heart becomes like God's.
Christ, greater than Jonah, calls us to listen.
2027-01-21.resolve: Reconcile with one person this week.

intro: Theme: “Fight the good fight of the faith.”
Mar Timotheos: the good fight, Christ's fulfilment, and faith handed on at home.

q: Be strong and bold; have no fear or dread of them, because it is the LORD your God who goes with you; he will not fail you or forsake you.”
Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of the eternal life, to which you were called and for which you made the good confession in the presence of many witnesses.
points.apply: Practise one of Paul's six virtues each day.

points.h: Not to abolish but to fulfil
sub: Reading the Old Testament in his light.
q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
“Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.
points.apply: Read one Old Testament reading this week and ask how it points to Christ.

q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you.
points.apply: Pray with your children or grandchildren tonight.

concl: Timothy fought the good fight in weakness.
Christ fulfils the Scriptures; families hand them on.
2027-01-22.resolve: Begin a daily family Bible reading.

intro: Theme: “The mediator of a better covenant.”
Christ our high priest, the reality behind every shadow, who opens our lips.

q: The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
Now the main point in what we are saying is this: we have such a high priest, one who is seated at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
points.apply: Pray tomorrow for departed priests by name.

q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
But Jesus has now obtained a more excellent ministry, and to that degree he is the mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted through better promises.
points.apply: Attend the Qurbono tomorrow with awareness of the heavenly liturgy.

q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy. For waters shall break forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert;
And when the demon had been cast out, the one who had been mute spoke; and the crowds were amazed and said, “Never has anything like this been seen in Israel.”
points.apply: Speak one word of witness this week.

concl: Christ is our high priest and the reality of every shadow.
He opens our lips; let us praise and pray for his priests.
2027-01-23.resolve: Pray daily for your parish priest.

intro: Theme: “That they may all be one… so that the world may believe.”
The persecutor transformed, and the prayer of Jesus for unity.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
But get up and enter the city, and you will be told what you are to do.”
points.apply: Pray for someone hostile to the faith.

q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
they only heard it said, “The one who formerly was persecuting us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy.”
points.apply: Share your own story of grace with someone.

points.h: That they may all be one
q: I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king over them all. Never again shall they be two nations, and never again shall they be divided into two kingdoms.
that they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
points.apply: Do one act of friendship toward Christians of another Church.

concl: Grace turns persecutors into apostles.
Unity among Christians lets the world see Christ.

intro: Theme: “Give… to God the things that are God's.”
A letter of Christ, competence from God, and faithful citizenship.

q: I will give them one heart, and put a new spirit within them; I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
and you show that you are a letter of Christ, prepared by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
points.apply: Let your conduct today be a letter of Christ.

q: He said to me, “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, says the LORD of hosts.
Not that we are competent of ourselves to claim anything as coming from us; our competence is from God,
points.apply: Begin your work with a prayer for God's help.

q: So God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.
They answered, “The emperor's.” Then he said to them, “Give therefore to the emperor the things that are the emperor's, and to God the things that are God's.”
points.apply: Pray for India and its leaders today.

concl: We are God's letter and God's image.
Faithful citizens, wholly belonging to God.
2027-01-26.resolve: Serve the common good in one concrete way this week.

intro: Theme: “Just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her.”
Christian marriage: mutual reverence, self-giving love, an unbroken bond.

q: And I will take you for my wife forever; I will take you for my wife in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love, and in mercy.
Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ.
points.apply: Serve your spouse or family humbly today.

q: Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm; for love is strong as death, passion fierce as the grave. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a raging flame.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her,
points.apply: Do something costly out of love for your family.

q: Therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh.
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.”
points.apply: Pray for a couple who are struggling.

concl: Marriage is an icon of Christ's love for the Church.
Let our homes be domestic churches.
2027-01-27.resolve: Pray together as a family every evening this week.

intro: Theme: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”
Faithful leaders, the unchanging Christ, and the Way to the Father.

q: For I the LORD do not change; therefore you, O children of Jacob, have not perished.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
points.apply: Bring one anxiety about change to the unchanging Christ.

q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.
points.apply: Share something with someone in need.

sub: No one comes but through me.
q: You show me the path of life. In your presence there is fullness of joy; in your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
points.apply: Pray for a priest who showed you the way.

concl: Christ does not change; he is the way home.
Praise, share, and remember those who led us.
2027-01-28.resolve: Pray each day this week for departed priests.

intro: Theme: “If it dies, it bears much fruit.”
The grain of wheat, the living sacrifice, and Mar Ignatius, God's wheat.

q: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
I appeal to you therefore, brothers and sisters, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.
points.apply: Offer your day's work to God this morning.

q: But Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!”
so we, who are many, are one body in Christ, and individually we are members one of another.
points.apply: Use one of your gifts for the parish this week.

q: May those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy. Those who go out weeping, bearing the seed for sowing, shall come home with shouts of joy, carrying their sheaves.
Very truly, I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
points.apply: Let go of one selfish attachment.

concl: To see Jesus is to see the grain that dies and bears fruit.
Like Mar Ignatius, let us become God's wheat.
2027-01-29.resolve: Make one hidden sacrifice each day this week.

intro: Theme: “The good person brings good things out of a good treasure.”
Self-examination, the tree and its fruit, and the heart as Christ's temple.

q: Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
Examine yourselves to see whether you are living in the faith. Test yourselves. Do you not realize that Jesus Christ is in you?—unless, indeed, you fail to meet the test!
points.apply: Make an examination of conscience tonight.

q: Blessed are those who trust in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD. They shall be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots by the stream. It shall not fear when heat comes, and its leaves shall stay green; in the year of drought it is not anxious, and it does not cease to bear fruit.
“Either make the tree good, and its fruit good; or make the tree bad, and its fruit bad; for the tree is known by its fruit.
points.apply: Root your day in ten minutes of prayer.

q: Set a guard over my mouth, O LORD; keep watch over the door of my lips.
I tell you, on the day of judgment you will have to give an account for every careless word you utter; for by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”
points.apply: Avoid one hurtful word today.

concl: Our words reveal our hearts.
Let Christ dwell in the temple of the heart, as Aphrahat taught.
2027-01-30.resolve: Make a good confession before next Sunday.
